incidents.title: The Sages of Naimisharanya
incidents.story: In the sacred forest of Naimisharanya, many sages gathered for a long sacrifice of a thousand years. Seeing the wise storyteller Suta among them, they asked him to tell the stories of Lord Krishna. Pleased, Suta began to recite the Bhagavatam, the purest of all sacred tales.
incidents.scene: sages seated in forest hermitage listening

incidents.title: Vyasa's Despondency
incidents.story: Vyasa had divided the Vedas and written the great Mahabharata for the good of all, yet his heart felt empty. Sitting alone by the river Sarasvati, he wondered what he had missed. Just then Narada arrived playing his vina, and told him that he had not yet fully sung the glories of the Lord.
incidents.scene: Vyasa seated by river with Narada

incidents.title: Narada's Previous Life
incidents.story: Narada told Vyasa of his own past life as the son of a poor maidservant. As a boy he served wandering sages during the rainy season, ate their leftover food and heard them sing of Hari. Their company slowly washed his heart clean and filled it with love for the Lord.
incidents.scene: young boy serving sages in hermitage

incidents.title: Narada Glimpses the Lord
incidents.story: After his mother died of a snakebite, the boy wandered alone into a deep forest. Meditating beneath a tree, he saw the Lord shining in his heart, but the vision soon vanished. A gentle voice promised he would see Him again in his next life, and so he was reborn as Narada.
incidents.scene: boy meditating under tree in forest

incidents.title: Vyasa Composes the Bhagavatam
incidents.story: Inspired by Narada's words, Vyasa sat in his hermitage at Shamyaprasa and fixed his mind on the Lord in pure devotion. In that clear vision he composed the Srimad Bhagavatam. He then taught it to his son Shuka, a sage already free from all worldly desire.
incidents.scene: Vyasa writing scripture in forest hermitage

incidents.title: Ashwatthama's Night Attack
incidents.story: After the great war, Ashwatthama crept into the Pandava camp at night, hoping to please the fallen Duryodhana. In the darkness he killed the five sleeping sons of Draupadi. When she woke to find her children slain, Draupadi wept with grief.
incidents.scene: warrior attacking sleeping camp at night

incidents.title: Draupadi Spares Ashwatthama
incidents.story: Arjuna chased Ashwatthama, defeated his deadly weapon with Krishna's help and dragged him bound before Draupadi. Though he had killed her sons, she pitied him as the son of their teacher Drona and begged that he be spared. Arjuna cut off the jewel from his head and drove him away.
incidents.scene: bound warrior brought before weeping queen

incidents.title: Parikshit Saved in the Womb
incidents.story: Still full of hate, Ashwatthama hurled the Brahmastra at the unborn child of Uttara, the last heir of the Pandavas. Terrified, Uttara ran to Krishna for shelter. Holding His discus, the Lord entered her womb and shielded the baby Parikshit from the blazing weapon.
incidents.scene: Krishna protecting frightened queen from weapon

incidents.title: Kunti's Prayer
incidents.story: As Krishna prepared to leave for Dwaraka, Queen Kunti stood before His chariot and prayed to Him with folded hands. She thanked Him for saving her family from every danger. She even asked for more troubles, because in times of trouble she always remembered Him.
incidents.scene: queen praying before Krishna's chariot

incidents.title: Bhishma's Passing
incidents.story: Grieving for the war, Yudhishthira went with Krishna to Bhishma, who lay on a bed of arrows at Kurukshetra. The old warrior taught him the duties of a king, then gazed lovingly at Krishna standing before him. Praying to the Lord, Bhishma peacefully gave up his body.
incidents.scene: Bhishma on bed of arrows

incidents.title: Krishna Returns to Dwaraka
incidents.story: With Yudhishthira settled on the throne, Krishna set out for Dwaraka as the women of Hastinapura sadly watched Him go. When He blew His conch at the city gates, the people of Dwaraka rushed out with gifts and joyful music. He entered the palace and greeted His elders and His queens.
incidents.scene: Krishna welcomed by citizens at city gates

incidents.title: The Birth of Parikshit
incidents.story: Uttara gave birth to a radiant son, the child the Lord had saved in the womb. The learned priests foretold that he would be a righteous king, as brave and kind as Rama. Because he seemed always to be searching for the Lord he had seen before birth, he was called Parikshit.
incidents.scene: royal infant blessed by priests in palace

incidents.title: Vidura Counsels Dhritarashtra
incidents.story: Vidura came back to Hastinapura after a long pilgrimage and was warmly welcomed. Seeing his blind elder brother Dhritarashtra still clinging to palace comforts, he spoke frankly. Death was near, he warned, so Dhritarashtra should leave home at once and seek the Lord.
incidents.scene: sage advising blind old king

incidents.title: Dhritarashtra Leaves for the Forest
incidents.story: Moved by Vidura's words, Dhritarashtra slipped away secretly at night with the faithful Gandhari. When Yudhishthira found them gone, he was heartbroken until Narada comforted him. Narada told him they were meditating in the Himalayas and would soon reach peace.
incidents.scene: blind king and queen walking into forest

incidents.title: Arjuna Brings Sad News
incidents.story: Yudhishthira noticed dark omens everywhere and grew worried for Krishna. Arjuna returned from Dwaraka pale and weeping, and told him that Krishna had left the world. Remembering all the Lord's kindness, Arjuna found peace again in the teachings of the Gita.
incidents.scene: grieving Arjuna before king Yudhishthira

incidents.title: The Pandavas Depart
incidents.story: Knowing that the age of Kali had begun, Yudhishthira crowned young Parikshit king of Hastinapura. Then he gave away his royal robes and walked north with his brothers and Draupadi, their minds fixed on Krishna. In this way the Pandavas reached the Lord's abode.
incidents.scene: Pandavas walking toward Himalayas

incidents.title: The Bull and the Cow
incidents.story: On a royal tour, Parikshit came upon a bull standing on one leg and a weeping cow. The bull was Dharma and the cow was Mother Earth, both mourning the Lord's departure. A cruel man dressed as a king was beating them with a club, and that man was Kali himself.
incidents.scene: king finding bull and cow beaten

incidents.title: Parikshit Spares Kali
incidents.story: Parikshit raised his sword to kill Kali, but Kali dropped his royal disguise and fell at his feet. The merciful king spared him and allowed him to live only in places of gambling, drinking, lust, slaughter and greed. He also healed the bull of Dharma, restoring his lost legs.
incidents.scene: king with sword over kneeling man

incidents.title: The Garland of the Dead Snake
incidents.story: Hunting one day, Parikshit grew tired and thirsty and entered the hermitage of the sage Shamika. The sage was deep in meditation and did not greet him. In a rare moment of anger, the king placed a dead snake around the sage's neck and returned to his palace.
incidents.scene: king placing snake on meditating sage

incidents.title: The Curse of Shringi
incidents.story: Shamika's young son Shringi heard how his father had been insulted. In boyish fury he cursed the king to die in seven days from the bite of the serpent Takshaka. Shamika woke, grieved that his son had cursed a good king, and sent word to Parikshit.
incidents.scene: angry boy cursing by river

incidents.title: Parikshit at the Ganga
incidents.story: Hearing of the curse, Parikshit felt it was a just reward for his offence. He gave his kingdom to his son Janamejaya and sat on the banks of the Ganga, fasting until death. Great sages from every corner of the land gathered around him there.
incidents.scene: king seated by Ganga among sages

incidents.title: Shuka Arrives
incidents.story: Into that great assembly walked young Shuka, son of Vyasa, wandering free and bright as the sun. All the sages rose to honour him, and Parikshit bowed at his feet. The king asked what a dying man should do, and Shuka began to tell him the Bhagavatam.
incidents.scene: young sage arriving before seated king

incidents.title: Shuka Begins His Teaching
incidents.story: Shuka praised Parikshit's question as the best one anyone could ask. He told the story of King Khatvanga, who learned he had only a moment left to live and gave his whole heart to the Lord. Seven days, Shuka said, are more than enough to reach the highest goal.
incidents.scene: sage teaching king by riverbank

incidents.title: The Universal Form
incidents.story: To help the king fix his mind on the Lord, Shuka described the Universal Form. The worlds below are His feet and the heavens are His head. The sun is His eye, the rivers are His veins, the mountains are His bones, and all creation lives within His vast body.
incidents.scene: cosmic form of Vishnu containing worlds

incidents.title: The Lord in the Heart
incidents.story: Shuka then taught a gentler meditation on the Lord dwelling within the heart. He is the size of a thumb, four-armed, holding the conch, discus, mace and lotus, wearing yellow silk and a garland of forest flowers. Seeing Him there, the yogi gives up the body in peace.
incidents.scene: four-armed Vishnu in lotus heart

incidents.title: Worship for Every Desire
incidents.story: Shuka told the king that people worship many gods for their wishes: Indra for strength, the Sun for health, Lakshmi for wealth. Yet the wise person, whether full of desires, free of them, or longing for liberation, should worship Lord Hari alone. A life without hearing His stories, he said, is a life wasted.
incidents.scene: sage instructing king among gathered sages

incidents.title: Narada Questions Brahma
incidents.story: Shuka recalled how Narada once asked his father Brahma who had truly created the world. Brahma humbly replied that it was not he. He was only a servant, he said, and it was Lord Narayana who gave him the power to create all beings and all worlds.
incidents.scene: Narada bowing before four-headed Brahma

incidents.title: The Cosmic Purusha
incidents.story: Brahma explained how the Lord as the cosmic Purusha lay upon the waters of the causal ocean. From Him came time, nature and all the elements. Entering the egg of the universe, He gave it life, and from His body the worlds, the gods and all beings came forth.
incidents.scene: Vishnu reclining on cosmic waters

incidents.title: The Avatars of the Lord
incidents.story: Brahma told Narada of the Lord's many avatars. He came as Varaha to lift the Earth, Matsya to save the Vedas and Kurma to hold up a mountain. He became Narasimha to protect Prahlada, Vamana to humble Bali, and Rama and Krishna to destroy evil and delight His devotees.
incidents.scene: ten avatars of Vishnu in panels

incidents.title: Brahma Hears Tapa
incidents.story: Seated on the lotus that grew from the Lord's navel, Brahma did not know how to begin creation. Then from the waters he heard a voice say two words, tapa, tapa, meaning austerity. Brahma obeyed and meditated with full focus for a thousand divine years.
incidents.scene: Brahma meditating on lotus over waters

incidents.title: Brahma's Vision of Vaikuntha
incidents.story: Pleased by his tapas, the Lord showed Brahma His own realm, Vaikuntha. There was no fear, no time and no illusion, and shining devotees flew in beautiful aerial cars. On a throne sat the Lord with Lakshmi, attended by His joyful companions.
incidents.scene: Vishnu and Lakshmi enthroned in Vaikuntha

incidents.title: The Four Verses
incidents.story: The Lord then taught Brahma the essence of all wisdom in four short verses. Before creation only He existed, and after it ends only He remains. Whatever seems apart from Him is illusion, and He is present both within and beyond all things.
incidents.scene: Vishnu teaching kneeling Brahma

incidents.title: Vidura Leaves Hastinapura
incidents.story: Vidura begged King Dhritarashtra to return the Pandavas their share of the kingdom and avoid ruin. Duryodhana insulted him and ordered him thrown out of the palace. Calm and without anger, Vidura left his bow at the door and set out on pilgrimage, thinking only of Krishna.
incidents.scene: Vidura leaving the Kaurava palace hall

incidents.title: Vidura Meets Uddhava
incidents.story: Wandering to holy places, Vidura met Uddhava, Krishna's dear friend, on the bank of the Yamuna. He eagerly asked after Krishna and the Yadavas. Overwhelmed by memories of his master, Uddhava could not speak for a long while, and tears of love streamed from his eyes.
incidents.scene: Vidura embracing Uddhava by the river

incidents.title: Uddhava Tells of Krishna's Departure
incidents.story: Uddhava told Vidura that the Yadava clan had perished in a quarrel at Prabhasa and that Krishna had left the world. Before going, Krishna had sat beneath a tree, taught Uddhava the highest wisdom, and sent him to Badarikashrama. He also asked that Vidura be taught by the sage Maitreya.
incidents.scene: Krishna seated under tree teaching Uddhava

incidents.title: Vidura Meets Maitreya
incidents.story: Vidura travelled to Haridwar, where he found the wise sage Maitreya on the bank of the Ganga. Bowing humbly, he asked why people seek happiness yet find sorrow, and how the Lord creates the universe. Pleased by his devotion, Maitreya began to tell him the story of creation.
incidents.scene: Vidura bowing to sage by Ganga

incidents.title: Vishnu Sleeps on Ananta
incidents.story: Before creation, the whole universe lay drowned in the waters of dissolution. Upon them the Lord Narayana rested on the great serpent Ananta, whose thousand hoods spread like a canopy of jewels. He seemed to sleep, yet within Him lay all the worlds and beings waiting to be born again.
incidents.scene: Vishnu reclining on serpent over cosmic ocean

incidents.title: Brahma Born on the Lotus
incidents.story: When the time for creation came, a golden lotus sprang from the navel of Vishnu, shining like the sun. Within it Brahma appeared, the four-headed creator. Looking in all directions with his four faces, he saw only endless water and wondered who he was and where he came from.
incidents.scene: Brahma seated on lotus from Vishnu's navel

incidents.title: Brahma Searches the Lotus Stem
incidents.story: Seeking the source of the lotus, Brahma entered its stem and went down into the dark waters for a hundred celestial years. He found no end and returned weary to his seat. Then he sat in silent meditation, and at last the Lord on Ananta appeared clearly within his heart.
incidents.scene: Brahma climbing down the lotus stalk

incidents.title: Brahma Prays to Vishnu
incidents.story: Seeing the radiant Lord reclining on Ananta, Brahma was filled with wonder and offered heartfelt prayers. He asked for the strength to create without pride. Smiling, Vishnu blessed him, told him to perform penance, and promised that devotion would keep him free from the bondage of his work.
incidents.scene: Four-headed Brahma praying to Vishnu on Ananta

incidents.title: Brahma Creates the Worlds
incidents.story: Strengthened by penance, Brahma divided the lotus into the three worlds and began to create. From his own body and mind came the many kinds of beings, from trees and animals to gods and humans. Maitreya explained to Vidura how time, from moments to vast ages, guides this great unfolding.
incidents.scene: Brahma creating worlds on a lotus

incidents.title: The Four Kumaras Refuse
incidents.story: Brahma first created four sons from his mind, the sages Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana and Sanatkumara. When he asked them to create offspring, they refused, wishing only to be devoted to the Lord. Brahma's anger blazed out from between his brows as Rudra, the blue and red child who wept as he was born.
incidents.scene: Four boy sages before Brahma

incidents.title: Manu and Shatarupa Appear
incidents.story: Still eager to fill the world with life, Brahma divided his own body into two. From one half came Svayambhuva Manu and from the other his queen Shatarupa. They became the first parents of humankind, and they humbly asked Brahma how they could best serve him and the Lord.
incidents.scene: First man and woman bowing to Brahma

incidents.title: Varaha Emerges from Brahma
incidents.story: Manu wished to rule, but the Earth had sunk deep beneath the cosmic waters. As Brahma wondered what to do, a tiny boar no bigger than a thumb sprang from his nostril. Within moments it grew as huge as a mountain and roared, and the sages knew that the Lord Himself had come.
incidents.scene: Tiny boar growing huge before Brahma

incidents.title: Varaha Lifts the Earth
incidents.story: The mighty boar Varaha plunged into the ocean, his bristles shaking and his hooves splitting the waters. Deep below he found the Earth, gently lifted her on his gleaming tusks, and rose up with her like the moon. The sages and Brahma sang his praises as he set the Earth upon the waters.
incidents.scene: Boar avatar lifting Earth on tusks

incidents.title: Diti Approaches Kashyapa at Dusk
incidents.story: Diti, the wife of the sage Kashyapa, longed for a son and came to him one evening. Kashyapa begged her to wait, since dusk was the hour when Shiva and his ghostly followers roam. Overcome by desire, she would not listen, and Kashyapa gave in, though he knew it would bring trouble.
incidents.scene: Sage and wife at sunset hermitage

incidents.title: Kashyapa's Prophecy
incidents.story: Ashamed, Diti prayed that her children would be spared. Kashyapa told her she would bear two fierce sons who would trouble the worlds and be slain by the Lord Himself. Yet because she repented, one of her grandsons, Prahlada, would become a great devotee loved by all.
incidents.scene: Sage consoling his sorrowful wife

incidents.title: Darkness Covers the Worlds
incidents.story: Fearing what her sons would do, Diti held them in her womb for a hundred years. Their power spread darkness everywhere, and the frightened gods went to Brahma for help. Brahma told them the cause lay in a curse given long ago at the gates of Vaikuntha, and he began to tell the story.
incidents.scene: Gods approaching Brahma in darkness

incidents.title: The Kumaras Reach Vaikuntha
incidents.story: The four Kumaras, eternal sages who look like small boys, travelled to Vaikuntha, the shining realm of Vishnu. They passed through six gates of jewelled palaces and gardens without stopping. At the seventh gate stood two splendid doorkeepers, Jaya and Vijaya, holding maces.
incidents.scene: Four boy sages at jewelled gates

incidents.title: The Curse of Jaya and Vijaya
incidents.story: Jaya and Vijaya mistook the Kumaras for mere children and barred their way with their staffs. The sages were angered that anyone should be blocked from the Lord, and cursed the guards to be born as demons on Earth. Realising their mistake, the doorkeepers fell at the sages' feet in fear.
incidents.scene: Boy sages cursing two gatekeepers

incidents.title: Vishnu Greets the Kumaras
incidents.story: Knowing what had happened, Vishnu came to the gate with Lakshmi, riding on Garuda. The scent of tulasi from His feet melted the sages' hearts, and they praised Him with joy. The Lord accepted the curse, and promised Jaya and Vijaya that after three demon births they would return to Him.
incidents.scene: Vishnu on Garuda meeting the Kumaras

incidents.title: Birth of the Demon Twins
incidents.story: At last Diti gave birth to twin sons, and terrible omens shook the worlds. The earth trembled, winds howled and comets blazed in the sky. Kashyapa named them Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha, and they quickly grew into giants whose heads seemed to touch the sky.
incidents.scene: Two giant demon brothers born amid omens

incidents.title: Hiranyaksha Challenges Varuna
incidents.story: Proud of his strength, Hiranyaksha roamed the worlds with his mace looking for a fight, and the gods hid in fear. He dived into the ocean and challenged Varuna, lord of the waters. Varuna calmly told him that only the Lord could match him, and that He would soon humble his pride.
incidents.scene: Demon with mace challenging sea god

incidents.title: Hiranyaksha Meets Varaha
incidents.story: Hiranyaksha went searching and found Varaha rising from the ocean with the Earth on his tusks. The demon mocked him as a mere forest animal and tried to stop him. Ignoring the insults, Varaha first set the Earth safely upon the waters, then turned to face the demon.
incidents.scene: Boar avatar carrying Earth facing demon

incidents.title: Varaha Slays Hiranyaksha
incidents.story: A fierce battle followed, mace against mace, while Brahma and the gods watched. When the demon used dark magic, the Lord broke it with his discus. At last Varaha struck Hiranyaksha below the ear and he fell like a great tree, and the gods showered flowers in joy.
incidents.scene: Varaha battling demon with mace

incidents.title: Kardama's Penance
incidents.story: Brahma told the sage Kardama to have children, so he performed penance for ten thousand years beside the Sarasvati river. Pleased, Vishnu appeared before him on Garuda and promised him a worthy wife. Tears of joy fell from the Lord's eyes, and the place became the holy lake Bindu Sarovara.
incidents.scene: Vishnu on Garuda appearing to meditating sage

incidents.title: Manu Gives Devahuti to Kardama
incidents.story: Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa travelled with their daughter Devahuti to Kardama's hermitage. Manu humbly offered her to the sage, saying she had chosen him in her heart. Kardama was pleased by her beauty and goodness, and the two were married beside the lake.
incidents.scene: King offering daughter to forest sage

incidents.title: Kardama's Flying Palace
incidents.story: Devahuti served her husband faithfully until she grew thin and weak. Pleased, Kardama created by yogic power a wondrous flying palace of jewels and gardens. Devahuti bathed in Bindu Sarovara, was attended by a thousand maidens, and travelled the heavens with him in great joy.
incidents.scene: Sage and wife in a flying jewelled palace

incidents.title: Birth of Kapila
incidents.story: Devahuti bore nine daughters, and later Vishnu Himself was born as her son, named Kapila. Brahma came with the sages to honour the divine child and told Kardama who he truly was. Kardama gave his daughters in marriage to great sages, who would fill the world with good families.
incidents.scene: Brahma blessing baby Kapila with parents

incidents.title: Kardama Renounces the World
incidents.story: Knowing his duty was done, Kardama bowed to his son Kapila and asked permission to leave home. Kapila blessed him and told him to fix his mind on the Lord in every being. Kardama went into the forest, free of all desire, and reached the Lord through devotion.
incidents.scene: Sage bowing to his son before leaving

incidents.title: Kapila Teaches Devahuti
incidents.story: Devahuti asked her son to free her from the darkness of worldly life. Kapila lovingly taught her how the self differs from matter, how the soul wanders from birth to birth, and how devotion to the Lord is the surest path to freedom. She listened closely, and her doubts melted away.
incidents.scene: Young sage teaching his seated mother

incidents.title: Devahuti Attains Liberation
incidents.story: After Kapila left for the north, Devahuti lived in the hermitage meditating on his form. She gave up all attachment, and her body became thin while her heart filled with peace. She attained the Lord, and the place became the holy Siddhapada, while the ocean itself gave Kapila a home.
incidents.scene: Woman meditating in a forest hermitage

incidents.title: Daksha Curses Shiva
incidents.story: At a great sacrifice of the Prajapatis, everyone rose to greet Daksha except Brahma and Shiva, who sat absorbed in meditation. Proud Daksha took this as an insult from his own son-in-law. In anger he cursed Shiva to receive no share of sacrificial offerings, and a bitter feud was born.
incidents.scene: Daksha cursing Shiva in sacrificial assembly

incidents.title: Sati Goes to Her Father
incidents.story: Seeing her sisters fly in celestial chariots to Daksha's grand sacrifice, Sati longed to go home. Shiva warned her that her father would only insult her, yet her love for her family won out. She set off on Nandi with Shiva's attendants, leaving her lord behind on Kailasa.
incidents.scene: Sati pleading with Shiva on Kailasa

incidents.title: Sati Gives Up Her Body
incidents.story: At the sacrifice, Daksha ignored his daughter and no share was set aside for Shiva. Hurt and furious, Sati rebuked her father before the assembly for hating the most auspicious lord. Refusing to keep a body born of him, she sat in yogic meditation and was consumed by inner fire.
incidents.scene: Sati burning in yogic fire at sacrifice

incidents.title: Shiva Creates Virabhadra
incidents.story: When Narada told Shiva of Sati's death, the lord rose in terrible anger. He tore a matted lock from his head and dashed it to the ground. From it sprang Virabhadra, a towering warrior black as storm clouds, with a thousand arms, burning eyes and a garland of skulls, ready to obey.
incidents.scene: Shiva tearing hair to create Virabhadra

incidents.title: Virabhadra Destroys the Sacrifice
incidents.story: Virabhadra and Shiva's ghostly hosts stormed Daksha's arena like a whirlwind. They smashed the pots, put out the fires and scattered the priests and gods. Virabhadra seized Daksha, cut off his proud head and offered it into the sacrificial fire, while all who had mocked Shiva fled.
incidents.scene: Virabhadra beheading Daksha at sacrifice

incidents.title: Brahma Pacifies Shiva
incidents.story: The shaken gods went with Brahma to Kailasa, where Shiva sat calm beneath a great banyan tree. Brahma praised him as the lord of all sacrifice and begged him to forgive Daksha. Shiva, quickly pleased, explained that Daksha's pride had brought its own punishment and agreed to restore everything.
incidents.scene: Brahma praying to Shiva under banyan

incidents.title: Daksha Receives a Goat's Head
incidents.story: By Shiva's grace, the head of the sacrificial goat was joined to Daksha's body, and he awoke humbled. He bowed to Shiva with tears of shame and love. As the sacrifice resumed, Lord Vishnu appeared on Garuda, and all praised him. Daksha completed his rite at last, free of envy.
incidents.scene: Goat-headed Daksha praying to Vishnu on Garuda

incidents.title: Dhruva Is Insulted
incidents.story: Little Dhruva, son of King Uttanapada and Queen Suniti, tried to climb onto his father's lap beside his half-brother Uttama. Queen Suruchi, the favored wife, pulled him away and said he must worship Vishnu and be born from her to sit there. The king said nothing, and Dhruva left in tears.
incidents.scene: Young Dhruva pushed from king's lap

incidents.title: Suniti Consoles Dhruva
incidents.story: Weeping, Dhruva ran to his gentle mother Suniti. She sighed that harsh as Suruchi's words were, they held a truth. She told her son to take shelter of Lord Vishnu, whose lotus feet even Brahma worships, for only the Lord could give him what he sought. The five-year-old resolved to go.
incidents.scene: Queen Suniti embracing weeping child Dhruva

incidents.title: Narada Meets Dhruva
incidents.story: On the road, the sage Narada met Dhruva and tested him, urging the small boy to return home and play. Dhruva firmly refused, wanting a place higher than any ancestor. Pleased, Narada taught him to meditate on Vishnu's beautiful form and chant a sacred mantra at Madhuvana by the Yamuna.
incidents.scene: Narada with veena blessing boy Dhruva

incidents.title: Dhruva's Austerity at Madhuvana
incidents.story: At Madhuvana, Dhruva fasted ever more strictly, living on fruits, then water, then air alone. In the sixth month he stood on one leg, fixing his mind wholly on the Lord. His concentration grew so powerful that the earth tilted and the breath of all beings was choked, and the gods ran to Vishnu.
incidents.scene: Dhruva meditating on one leg in forest

incidents.title: Vishnu Appears to Dhruva
incidents.story: Lord Vishnu came to Madhuvana on Garuda, and the vision in Dhruva's heart suddenly stood before his eyes. Speechless with joy, the boy could not praise him. Vishnu gently touched his cheek with his conch, and divine words poured forth. The Lord promised him a kingdom and then the eternal Pole Star.
incidents.scene: Vishnu touching Dhruva's cheek with conch

incidents.title: Dhruva Returns Home
incidents.story: Dhruva returned regretting he had asked the Lord only for a kingdom. Hearing he was coming, King Uttanapada rode out in a golden chariot with both queens, and the city was decorated with banners and flowers. The king embraced his son, Suruchi blessed him, and in time Dhruva was crowned king.
incidents.scene: King embracing Dhruva in festive procession

incidents.title: Dhruva Battles the Yakshas
incidents.story: When his brother Uttama was killed by a Yaksha while hunting in the Himalayas, Dhruva rode in fury to Alakapuri. Alone on his chariot he faced vast hosts of Yakshas and their magic illusions of fire, rain and monsters. He fixed a weapon of Narayana to his bow and slew them by the thousands.
incidents.scene: Dhruva fighting Yakshas from chariot

incidents.title: Manu Calms Dhruva
incidents.story: Seeing his grandson slaughtering innocent Yakshas, Svayambhuva Manu came with the sages. He gently told Dhruva that anger is the enemy of devotion and that the Yakshas were not the real cause of his brother's death. Dhruva bowed to his grandfather and at once laid down his arms.
incidents.scene: Manu counseling Dhruva on battlefield

incidents.title: Kuvera Blesses Dhruva
incidents.story: Kuvera, lord of riches and king of the Yakshas, was pleased that Dhruva had given up his anger. He came before him and offered any boon he wished. Dhruva asked only for unbroken remembrance of Lord Hari. Kuvera granted it gladly, and Dhruva returned to rule justly for many thousands of years.
incidents.scene: Kuvera granting boon to Dhruva

incidents.title: Dhruva Ascends to the Pole Star
incidents.story: When Dhruva retired to Badarikashrama, a shining airplane descended with two messengers of Vishnu. Dhruva stepped on the head of death itself to climb aboard. Remembering his mother, he saw Suniti flying ahead of him. He rose past all the planets to Dhruvaloka, the Pole Star around which they turn.
incidents.scene: Dhruva rising in celestial airplane

incidents.title: King Anga Leaves His Kingdom
incidents.story: Pious King Anga had a cruel son, Vena, who drowned playmates and slew animals for sport. Grieved and unable to correct him, Anga quietly left the palace at night and vanished into the forest. The sages then placed Vena on the throne, hoping power would teach him duty, but he grew worse.
incidents.scene: King Anga leaving palace at night

incidents.title: The Sages Slay Vena
incidents.story: Vena declared himself the only god and banned all worship and sacrifice. The sages humbly begged him to honor Vishnu, but he insulted them. In righteous anger they struck him dead with sacred sounds alone. Without a king, robbers soon roamed the land, and the sages saw the world in danger.
incidents.scene: Sages cursing the wicked King Vena

incidents.title: Prithu Is Born
incidents.story: To save the dynasty, the sages churned dead Vena's body. From his thighs came a dark dwarf, Nishada, who took away the king's sins. Then from his arms arose a radiant pair, Prithu and Archi, a partial incarnation of Vishnu and of Lakshmi. Gods and sages showered flowers and crowned Prithu.
incidents.scene: Prithu and Archi emerging from Vena's arms

incidents.title: Prithu Pursues the Earth
incidents.story: Under Vena the earth had hidden her grains and herbs, and people starved. Angry, King Prithu took up his bow to strike her. Trembling, the earth took the form of a cow and fled across the worlds, but found no refuge. At last she turned, bowed, and begged the king to hear her plea.
incidents.scene: Prithu with bow chasing earth cow

incidents.title: Prithu Milks the Earth
incidents.story: The earth explained that she had withheld her wealth from wicked men and asked for a calf and level ground. Prithu made Manu the calf and milked her into his own hands, drawing out every grain. Then gods, sages, demons and serpents each milked her in turn, and Prithu leveled the land for towns.
incidents.scene: Prithu milking the earth as cow

incidents.title: Indra Steals the Horse
incidents.story: Prithu began a hundred horse sacrifices, and jealous Indra feared losing his fame. Disguised as a holy mendicant, he stole the sacrificial horse. Prithu's son chased him, and Indra dropped the horse and fled, inventing false orders of ascetics as he went. Brahma persuaded Prithu to stop at ninety-nine.
incidents.scene: Indra disguised as ascetic stealing horse

incidents.title: Vishnu Blesses Prithu
incidents.story: Lord Vishnu arrived at Prithu's sacrifice with Indra, who stood ashamed. The Lord praised Prithu's patience and urged him to forgive. Prithu embraced Indra and then worshiped the Lord, asking for no boon but ten thousand ears to hear his glories. Vishnu was delighted and blessed him with devotion.
incidents.scene: Vishnu blessing King Prithu with Indra

incidents.title: Kumaras Instruct Prithu
incidents.story: One day the four boy sages, the Kumaras, descended from the sky, glowing like fire. Prithu honored them with water, seats and humble words. Sanat Kumara taught him that the highest goal is love for the Lord's lotus feet, which cuts the knot of false ego. Grateful, Prithu offered them his kingdom.
incidents.scene: Four boy sages instructing King Prithu

incidents.title: Prithu and Archi Depart
incidents.story: In old age Prithu gave his kingdom to his sons and went to the forest with his wife Archi. He lived on fruits and air, absorbed in the Lord, and finally gave up his body in yoga. Faithful Archi built his funeral pyre by the river, bathed, and entered the flames to follow her husband.
incidents.scene: Queen Archi at King Prithu's pyre

incidents.title: Prachetas Meet Shiva
incidents.story: The ten sons of King Prachinabarhi, called the Prachetas, set out to perform austerities. Beside a lovely lake they met Lord Shiva with his followers. Pleased with their devotion, Shiva taught them a beautiful prayer to Vishnu. The brothers then entered the ocean and chanted it for ten thousand years.
incidents.scene: Shiva teaching prayer to ten princes

incidents.title: Puranjana Meets the Queen
incidents.story: Narada told King Prachinabarhi a parable. King Puranjana wandered until he found a city of nine gates, where a beautiful young woman walked with her ten servants and a five-headed serpent. They married and enjoyed life, and Narada revealed that the city was the body and Puranjana the soul.
incidents.scene: King Puranjana meeting queen in garden

incidents.title: Puranjana Reborn as Vaidarbhi
incidents.story: In the parable, old age and the soldiers of time besieged Puranjana's city and set it ablaze. Dying with his mind fixed on his wife, he was reborn as Vaidarbhi, a princess. After her husband's death, an old friend appeared and revealed he was her eternal companion, the Lord, waiting all along.
incidents.scene: Princess weeping at husband's funeral pyre

incidents.title: Prachetas Marry Marisha
incidents.story: Emerging from the sea, the Prachetas saw trees covering the earth and burned them with fire and wind from their mouths. Soma, king of plants, calmed them and offered the lovely Marisha, raised by the trees, as their bride. From her was born a son, Daksha reborn, who peopled the worlds again.
incidents.scene: Ten princes marrying maiden Marisha

incidents.title: Priyavrata Accepts the Throne
incidents.story: Prince Priyavrata, son of Svayambhuva Manu, wanted only to meditate on the Lord under Narada's guidance. Brahma came down on his swan with the sages and gently told him that ruling was also the Lord's will. Priyavrata humbly agreed, and Manu gladly gave him the earth and retired to the forest.
incidents.scene: Brahma on swan advising Prince Priyavrata

incidents.title: Priyavrata Makes Seven Seas
incidents.story: Unhappy that the sun lit only half the world at a time, King Priyavrata drove a blazing chariot seven times around the earth, as bright as the sun itself. The ruts of its wheels became the seven oceans, and the land between them became the seven islands, which he gave to his seven sons.
incidents.scene: Blazing chariot circling the earth

incidents.title: Agnidhra and Purvachitti
incidents.story: Priyavrata's son Agnidhra, king of Jambudvipa, worshiped Brahma on a mountain hoping for a son. Brahma sent the apsara Purvachitti, who wandered nearby, charming him with her beauty and the hum of the bees. Enchanted, Agnidhra praised her and won her as his wife, and she bore him nine sons.
incidents.scene: King meeting apsara in flowering garden

incidents.title: Lord Appears at Nabhi's Sacrifice
incidents.story: Agnidhra's son King Nabhi and Queen Merudevi had no child, so they worshiped Lord Vishnu in a great sacrifice. Pleased, the Lord appeared in four-armed golden form. The priests prayed for a son as good as the Lord himself, and since none is equal to him, Vishnu chose to be born as their son.
incidents.scene: Vishnu appearing at King Nabhi's sacrifice

incidents.title: Rishabhadeva Instructs His Sons
incidents.story: Lord Rishabhadeva, born to Nabhi and Merudevi, ruled so wisely that the people wanted no other king. Before leaving the world, he gathered his hundred sons and taught them that human life is not meant for hard labor for sense pleasure, but for austerity, service to saints and love of God.
incidents.scene: Rishabhadeva teaching his hundred sons

incidents.title: Rishabhadeva the Wandering Sage
incidents.story: Giving his kingdom to his eldest son Bharata, Rishabhadeva left with nothing but his body, naked and silent like a madman. People mocked and abused him, but he stayed in bliss, his body fragrant with divine scent. At last, wandering in South India, he entered a forest fire and left the world.
incidents.scene: Naked ascetic wandering through forest

incidents.title: Bharata and the Deer
incidents.story: Emperor Bharata, after whom India is named, retired to Pulaha ashrama on the Gandaki river. One day a pregnant doe, frightened by a lion's roar, leapt across the river and gave birth, then died. Bharata rescued the orphaned fawn and raised it tenderly, until his love for it eclipsed his meditation.
incidents.scene: Sage Bharata cradling fawn by river

incidents.title: Bharata Reborn as a Deer
incidents.story: Bharata died gazing at his beloved deer, which stood weeping beside him. As he thought of it at death, he was born as a deer in the Kalanjara mountains. Yet he remembered his past and his mistake. He left his mother, returned alone to Pulaha ashrama, and waited peacefully for his next birth.
incidents.scene: Lone deer near forest ashrama

incidents.title: Jada Bharata Saved by Kali
incidents.story: Reborn a brahmana, Bharata acted dull and silent to avoid attachment, so people called him Jada, the dullard. Robbers seized him as a human offering to Goddess Bhadrakali. As the knife was raised, the goddess burst from the image in fury, beheaded the robbers, and saved the saintly boy.
incidents.scene: Goddess Kali killing robbers before temple

incidents.title: Jada Bharata Carries the Palanquin
incidents.story: King Rahugana's bearers forced Jada Bharata to carry the royal palanquin. He walked carefully to avoid stepping on ants, making the ride bumpy. The king mocked him, and Jada Bharata calmly replied with deep teachings on body and soul. Stunned, Rahugana leapt down and begged forgiveness.
incidents.scene: Sage carrying king's palanquin

incidents.title: Mount Meru and Jambudvipa
incidents.story: Shukadeva describes the earth as a vast lotus. At its center lies Jambudvipa, with golden Mount Meru rising in its midst like the seed pod of the flower. Around it lie nine regions and great mountains, gardens and lakes of milk, honey and nectar, and the realm of Bharata-varsha to the south.
incidents.scene: Golden Mount Meru at lotus center

incidents.title: Ganga Descends on Meru
incidents.story: When Lord Vamana raised his foot to measure the worlds, his toenail pierced the shell of the universe, and the Ganga flowed in, washing his lotus feet. She descended to Dhruvaloka, where Dhruva bears her on his head, then fell upon Mount Meru and divided into four rivers.
incidents.scene: Ganga flowing from Vishnu's foot

incidents.title: The Sun's Chariot
incidents.story: The sun god moves across the sky in a chariot with a single wheel, drawn by seven horses named after the Vedic meters, with Aruna as charioteer. Sixty thousand tiny sages called Valakhilyas walk before him chanting prayers, and his path divides the year into seasons, days and nights.
incidents.scene: Sun god in seven-horse chariot

incidents.title: Ananta Holds the Universe
incidents.story: Far below the lower worlds rests Lord Ananta, also called Sankarshana, the thousand-headed serpent form of Vishnu. The whole universe sits on one of his hoods like a mustard seed. Serpent maidens worship him, and at the end of time his anger brings forth the fire that dissolves creation.
incidents.scene: Thousand-headed serpent Ananta holding universe

incidents.title: Ajamila Calls Narayana
incidents.story: Ajamila, once a dutiful brahmana of Kanyakubja, fell into bad company and lived by cheating and theft. In old age he doted on his youngest son, whom he had named Narayana. As he lay dying, three fearsome messengers of Yama came with ropes, and in terror he cried out his son's name, Narayana.
incidents.scene: dying man terrified by Yama's messengers

incidents.title: Vishnudutas Rescue Ajamila
incidents.story: At that very cry, shining messengers of Vishnu appeared and stopped Yama's servants. When the Yamadutas protested that Ajamila was a great sinner, the Vishnudutas explained that chanting the Lord's name, even unknowingly, wipes away every sin. They freed him and vanished.
incidents.scene: Vishnu's messengers confronting Yama's servants

incidents.title: Ajamila Goes to Haridwar
incidents.story: Ajamila awoke from death's door, deeply ashamed of his wasted life. Remembering the radiant beings who had saved him, he left home and went to Haridwar on the Ganga. There he fixed his mind on the Lord, and when he left his body, a golden chariot carried him to Vaikuntha.
incidents.scene: sage meditating by Ganga, golden chariot

incidents.title: Yama Instructs His Messengers
incidents.story: Puzzled and humbled, the Yamadutas asked their master Yama who could overrule him. Yama explained that Lord Vishnu rules all, and that the chanting of His holy name is the highest dharma. He told them never to go near devotees of the Lord, for even he bows to them.
incidents.scene: Yama on throne addressing his servants

incidents.title: Daksha's Hamsaguhya Prayers
incidents.story: To increase creation, Daksha performed great austerities on a mountain near the Vindhyas and offered beautiful prayers called the Hamsaguhya. Pleased, Lord Vishnu appeared before him on Garuda with eight arms, and gave him Asikni, daughter of Panchajana, as his wife.
incidents.scene: Vishnu on Garuda appearing to sage

incidents.title: Narada Teaches the Haryashvas
incidents.story: Daksha and Asikni had ten thousand sons, the Haryashvas, whom he sent to perform penance so they might populate the world. At the holy lake Narayana Saras, Narada met them and spoke in riddles about the soul and the world. Understanding his meaning, they gave up worldly life and never returned.
incidents.scene: Narada speaking to young ascetics by lake

incidents.title: The Shabalashvas Follow
incidents.story: Undaunted, Daksha fathered a thousand more sons, the Shabalashvas, and sent them to the same holy lake for penance. Narada came again and gently reminded them of their brothers' path. They too turned away from worldly duties and followed their elder brothers in search of the Lord.
incidents.scene: Narada with ascetic youths at sacred lake

incidents.title: Daksha Curses Narada
incidents.story: Hearing that all his sons had become renunciants, Daksha burned with grief and anger. He rebuked Narada harshly and cursed him to wander the worlds forever, never staying long in one place. The saintly Narada calmly accepted the curse, and Daksha went on to father sixty daughters.
incidents.scene: angry king cursing sage with vina

incidents.title: Indra Offends Brihaspati
incidents.story: Proud of his wealth, Indra sat on his throne with Shachi and failed to rise when his guru Brihaspati entered the assembly. Brihaspati silently left and disappeared. Without his guidance the devas were defeated by the asuras, and Brahma advised them to take Vishvarupa as their priest.
incidents.scene: Indra enthroned ignoring guru entering hall

incidents.title: Vishvarupa Gives the Narayana Kavacha
incidents.story: Vishvarupa, the learned three headed son of Tvashta, agreed to serve the devas as their priest. He taught Indra the Narayana Kavacha, a sacred armour of prayer calling on Lord Vishnu for protection in every direction. Protected by it, Indra conquered the asuras and regained his kingdom.
incidents.scene: three-headed priest teaching Indra

incidents.title: Indra Slays Vishvarupa
incidents.story: Vishvarupa's mother came from the asuras, and during sacrifices he secretly offered oblations to them too. When Indra learned of this, he cut off Vishvarupa's three heads, which turned into birds. Burdened by the sin of killing a brahmana, Indra shared it out among the earth, water, trees and women.
incidents.scene: Indra beheading three-headed sage, birds flying

incidents.title: Vritrasura Rises From the Fire
incidents.story: Grieving for his son, Tvashta offered a fire sacrifice to create an enemy for Indra. From the flames rose Vritrasura, a dark giant as tall as a mountain, with hair like burnished copper and eyes blazing like the midday sun. He covered the sky, and the devas' weapons were simply swallowed up.
incidents.scene: giant demon rising from sacrificial fire

incidents.title: Dadhichi Gives His Bones
incidents.story: The terrified devas prayed to Lord Vishnu, who told them to ask the sage Dadhichi for his body. Smiling, Dadhichi said the body is meant to serve others, and gave up his life in meditation. From his strong bones Vishvakarma fashioned the thunderbolt, the vajra, for Indra.
incidents.scene: sage giving his body to the gods

incidents.title: Vritrasura's Devotion
incidents.story: Vritrasura met Indra in battle, yet spoke not with hatred but with deep wisdom and longing for the Lord. When Indra's thunderbolt fell from his hand, Vritra told him to pick it up and fight on. Losing an arm, the giant swallowed Indra and his elephant Airavata whole.
incidents.scene: giant demon battling Indra on elephant

incidents.title: Indra Slays Vritrasura
incidents.story: Protected by the Narayana Kavacha, Indra cut his way out of Vritra's belly and severed his head with the thunderbolt. A light rose from the demon and merged into the Lord, for Vritra was a true devotee. Haunted by sin, Indra hid in a lotus stem in Manasa lake until purified by a horse sacrifice.
incidents.scene: Indra with thunderbolt slaying fallen giant

incidents.title: Chitraketu's Son Speaks
incidents.story: King Chitraketu had many wives but no son, until the sage Angira blessed his eldest queen. Jealous co-wives poisoned the baby, and the king was crushed with grief. Narada called back the child's soul, who said he had had countless parents in countless births, and the king found peace.
incidents.scene: grieving king, sages and dead child

incidents.title: Parvati Curses Chitraketu
incidents.story: By Narada's teaching Chitraketu became a king of the Vidyadharas and flew through the heavens. Seeing Shiva embracing Parvati before an assembly of sages, he laughed openly. Parvati cursed him to be born a demon, and he calmly accepted it, later becoming Vritrasura.
incidents.scene: Shiva and Parvati in assembly, king laughing

incidents.title: Diti and the Maruts
incidents.story: Diti longed for a son who would kill Indra, and Kashyapa gave her a year long vow. One evening she slept without washing her feet, and Indra entered her womb and cut the child into forty nine pieces. Yet by the vow's power they lived, became the Maruts, and were friends of Indra.
incidents.scene: Indra and Diti with storm gods

incidents.title: Yudhishthira Asks About Shishupala
incidents.story: At Yudhishthira's Rajasuya sacrifice, Shishupala insulted Krishna and was slain, yet his soul merged into the Lord. Amazed, Yudhishthira asked Narada how such an enemy could attain liberation. Narada explained that fixing the mind on the Lord, even through hatred, can purify the soul.
incidents.scene: king questioning sage in royal assembly

incidents.title: Jaya and Vijaya Are Cursed
incidents.story: Narada told how the four Kumaras, appearing as small boys, came to see Vishnu in Vaikuntha. The gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya blocked their way, so the sages cursed them to be born as demons. They were born as Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha, then Ravana and Kumbhakarna, then Shishupala and Dantavakra.
incidents.scene: child sages at Vaikuntha gates

incidents.title: Hiranyakashipu Vows Revenge
incidents.story: When Lord Varaha slew his brother Hiranyaksha, Hiranyakashipu bit his lip in fury and vowed to kill Vishnu. He sent his demons to harass sages and burn villages. Yet he gently consoled his grieving mother and relatives, telling them the soul never dies.
incidents.scene: furious demon king commanding his army

incidents.title: Hiranyakashipu's Fierce Tapas
incidents.story: Wishing to become immortal and unconquerable, Hiranyakashipu went to Mount Mandara and stood on tiptoe with arms raised, for years without moving. Ants and grass covered his body, and the fire of his penance scorched the worlds. The terrified devas ran to Brahma for help.
incidents.scene: demon in penance covered by anthill

incidents.title: Brahma Grants the Boon
incidents.story: Brahma came on his swan and sprinkled water on the anthill, restoring the demon's body. Hiranyakashipu asked that no being Brahma created could kill him, not by day or night, indoors or out, on earth or sky, nor by any weapon, man or beast. Brahma granted every word.
incidents.scene: Brahma on swan blessing kneeling demon

incidents.title: Hiranyakashipu Rules the Worlds
incidents.story: Proud of his boon, Hiranyakashipu conquered the three worlds and sat on Indra's throne, served by gods and sages. He forced all to worship him and ignored the laws of dharma. The devas prayed to Vishnu, who promised to end his tyranny when he harmed his own saintly son.
incidents.scene: demon king on heavenly throne

incidents.title: Prahlada in School
incidents.story: Hiranyakashipu's young son Prahlada was taught politics and power by Shanda and Amarka, sons of Shukracharya. But the boy saw everyone as equal and loved only Lord Vishnu. When his father asked what was best, Prahlada said to leave the false home and take shelter of Hari.
incidents.scene: young prince studying with demon teachers

incidents.title: Prahlada Answers His Father
incidents.story: Later, sitting on his father's lap, Prahlada was asked again what he had learned. He replied that the best learning is devotion to Vishnu, by hearing, chanting, remembering and serving Him. Furious, Hiranyakashipu threw the boy to the ground and ordered him killed.
incidents.scene: demon king throwing son from lap

incidents.title: Attempts to Kill Prahlada
incidents.story: The demons struck Prahlada with tridents, but the weapons failed, for his mind rested on the Lord. He was trampled by elephants, bitten by snakes, thrown from cliffs, poisoned, starved and cast into fire and water. Through it all he remained calm and unharmed.
incidents.scene: boy unharmed among elephants and snakes

incidents.title: Prahlada Teaches His Classmates
incidents.story: While his teachers were away, Prahlada gathered the demon boys and spoke to them with great love. He told them to begin devotion to Vishnu in childhood, since life is short and the Lord lives in every heart. Charmed by his words, the boys turned away from their teachers' lessons.
incidents.scene: boy prince teaching circle of children

incidents.title: Narada Shelters Kayadhu
incidents.story: Prahlada told how, while his father was away at penance, Indra seized his mother Kayadhu. Narada stopped Indra, saying her unborn child was a great devotee, and took her to his ashram. There he taught her the path of bhakti, and the child in her womb remembered every word.
incidents.scene: sage sheltering pregnant queen in ashram

incidents.title: Narasimha Bursts From the Pillar
incidents.story: Raging, Hiranyakashipu asked Prahlada where his God was, and the boy said He is everywhere. "Is He in this pillar?" roared the king, and struck it with his fist. With a terrible roar the Lord burst out as Narasimha, half man and half lion, proving his devotee's words true.
incidents.scene: man-lion emerging from shattered pillar

incidents.title: Narasimha Slays Hiranyakashipu
incidents.story: Narasimha seized the demon and carried him to the doorway at twilight, neither day nor night. Placing him on His thighs, neither earth nor sky, He tore him apart with His claws, which were no weapon. Every condition of Brahma's boon was kept, and the gods showered flowers.
incidents.scene: Narasimha tearing demon on lap at doorway

incidents.title: Prahlada Calms Narasimha
incidents.story: Narasimha's fury was so fearsome that even Brahma, Shiva and Lakshmi dared not approach Him. Brahma sent little Prahlada, who bowed at His feet. The Lord placed His hand on the boy's head, and Prahlada offered heartfelt prayers that slowly calmed His anger.
incidents.scene: child bowing before seated man-lion

incidents.title: Prahlada Asks for No Boon
incidents.story: Narasimha offered Prahlada any blessing, but the boy said a true servant wants nothing in return. He asked only that his father be forgiven, and the Lord said twenty one generations of his family were purified. Prahlada was then crowned king of the asuras.
incidents.scene: Narasimha blessing boy king

incidents.title: Shiva Destroys Tripura
incidents.story: Narada told how Maya Danava built three flying cities for the asuras, and Maya revived their dead in a well of nectar. Vishnu became a cow and Brahma a calf, and drank the well dry. Then Shiva, on a chariot made by the Lord, burned the three cities with a single arrow.
incidents.scene: Shiva on chariot shooting arrow at cities

incidents.title: Narada on Varnashrama
incidents.story: Yudhishthira asked Narada about the eternal duties of human life. Narada described the qualities of a good person, such as truth, mercy and self control, and the duties of each class and stage of life. Above all, he said, every duty should be offered to the Lord.
incidents.scene: sage instructing king and brothers

incidents.title: Prahlada Meets the Avadhuta
incidents.story: Narada told how Prahlada, wandering the world, found a saint lying in the dust by the Kaveri river. The saint said he lived like the python, eating whatever came, and like the honeybee, gathering wisdom everywhere. Free of desire, he was full of peace, and Prahlada honoured him.
incidents.scene: prince bowing to saint lying on ground

incidents.title: Yajna Protects Svayambhuva Manu
incidents.story: Svayambhuva Manu, the first father of mankind, gave up his kingdom and went to the forest to meditate on the Lord. Hungry demons rushed to devour him as he prayed. The Lord appeared as Yajna, slew the demons and ruled the heavens, the first of the protectors who guard each age of the Manus.
incidents.scene: Sage king meditating in forest hermitage

incidents.title: Gajendra Seized by the Crocodile
incidents.story: On Mount Trikuta lived Gajendra, mighty king of elephants. One hot day he led his herd into a lotus lake to bathe and play. Suddenly a powerful crocodile seized his leg. For a thousand years they struggled, until the great elephant grew weak and his family could not save him.
incidents.scene: Elephant in lotus lake seized by crocodile

incidents.title: Gajendra Prays to the Lord
incidents.story: Exhausted and helpless, Gajendra remembered a prayer from his past life. Lifting a lotus in his trunk, he praised the Supreme Lord, the source of all, beyond every form and name. He did not call on any lesser god, but surrendered fully to the one who shelters all who seek refuge.
incidents.scene: Elephant raising lotus flower toward sky

incidents.title: Vishnu Rescues Gajendra
incidents.story: Hearing his devotee's cry, Vishnu rushed from Vaikuntha on Garuda, the gods following behind. He pulled Gajendra and the crocodile out of the lake together. With his Sudarshana discus he cut open the crocodile's jaws, freeing the elephant, who was touched by the Lord's own hand.
incidents.scene: Vishnu on Garuda rescuing elephant

incidents.title: Indradyumna and Huhu Freed
incidents.story: The crocodile was really Huhu, a Gandharva cursed by the sage Devala, and he rose freed in his shining form. Gajendra had once been King Indradyumna, cursed by Agastya for failing to greet him. Touched by the Lord, he too was freed, and became an associate of Vishnu in Vaikuntha.
incidents.scene: Elephant transformed into four-armed devotee

incidents.title: Vishnu Counsels the Devas
incidents.story: Defeated by the demons, the gods lost their glory and went with Brahma to pray to the Lord. Vishnu appeared and told them to make a truce with the asuras and churn the ocean of milk for nectar. Together they lifted Mount Mandara, and when it crushed them, Garuda carried it to the shore.
incidents.scene: Gods and demons carrying a great mountain

incidents.title: Kurma Holds Mount Mandara
incidents.story: With the serpent Vasuki as the rope, gods and demons began to churn, but the heavy mountain sank into the sea. The Lord took the form of Kurma, a giant tortoise, and held Mandara on his vast back. He also entered the mountain and the churners, giving them strength to keep going.
incidents.scene: Giant tortoise holding mountain in ocean

incidents.title: The Halahala Poison Arises
incidents.story: As the churning went on, a terrible poison called Halahala rose from the ocean. Its fumes spread in every direction, burning the worlds, and gods and demons alike fled in fear. With no other shelter, the frightened beings ran to Lord Shiva on Mount Kailasa and begged him to protect them.
incidents.scene: Dark poison spreading over churning ocean

incidents.title: Shiva Drinks the Halahala
incidents.story: Moved by compassion, Shiva gathered the poison in his palm and drank it, with Parvati's blessing. The poison left a blue mark on his throat, and he became known as Nilakantha, the blue-throated one. The worlds praised him, for great souls take on suffering to relieve the suffering of others.
incidents.scene: Shiva drinking poison with blue throat

incidents.title: Treasures Rise From the Ocean
incidents.story: The churning went on, and wonders rose from the sea. The wish-fulfilling cow Surabhi came first, then the white horse Ucchaihshrava and the elephant Airavata. The Kaustubha gem, which Vishnu wore on his chest, the Parijata tree and the lovely Apsaras followed, each given to its rightful keeper.
incidents.scene: White elephant and horse rising from sea

incidents.title: Lakshmi Chooses Vishnu
incidents.story: Then Lakshmi, the goddess of fortune, rose from the ocean, radiant on a lotus. Rivers, sages and gods offered her worship and gifts. She looked over all the beings, finding faults in each, and at last placed her garland on Vishnu, the only one free from every flaw, and took her place on his chest.
incidents.scene: Goddess on lotus garlanding Vishnu

incidents.title: Dhanvantari Brings the Nectar
incidents.story: Varuni, goddess of wine, rose next and went to the demons. Then a dark, handsome youth appeared, wearing earrings and yellow silk and carrying a pot full of nectar. He was Dhanvantari, a part of the Lord and the founder of medicine. At once the demons snatched the pot of nectar from his hands.
incidents.scene: Divine physician rising with nectar pot

incidents.title: Mohini Distributes the Nectar
incidents.story: As the demons quarrelled over the pot, Vishnu appeared as Mohini, an enchanting woman. Charmed, they handed her the nectar to share. She seated gods and demons in separate rows and, with sweet glances, served the nectar only to the gods, while the bewitched demons waited in silence.
incidents.scene: Enchanting woman serving nectar to gods

incidents.title: Rahu Loses His Head
incidents.story: The demon Rahu disguised himself as a god and sat between the Sun and Moon to drink the nectar. When they exposed him, the Lord cut off his head with the discus. But the nectar had touched his lips, so the head lived on, and it still chases the Sun and Moon at the time of eclipses.
incidents.scene: Discus beheading demon among seated gods

incidents.title: War of the Gods and Demons
incidents.story: Cheated of the nectar, the demons attacked the gods in a fierce battle by the sea. Bali fought from a magic flying chariot, and the demons used terrible illusions. Vishnu came on Garuda and turned the tide. Indra struck down Bali and slew Namuchi with foam, until Narada asked the gods to stop.
incidents.scene: Gods and demons battling by the ocean

incidents.title: Shiva Sees Mohini
incidents.story: Hearing of Mohini, Shiva came with Parvati and asked Vishnu to show him that form. In a garden appeared a beautiful woman playing with a ball. Shiva was so charmed that he ran after her, forgetting himself. When he came to his senses, he praised the Lord's power of illusion, which bewilders even him.
incidents.scene: Shiva chasing woman playing with ball

incidents.title: Bali Conquers Heaven
incidents.story: Revived by Shukracharya and the Bhrigu sages, Bali performed the Vishvajit sacrifice and received a golden chariot and divine weapons. With a vast army he besieged Indra's city. Seeing his power, the gods fled in disguise, and Bali ruled the three worlds, performing a hundred great sacrifices.
incidents.scene: Demon king leading army against heaven

incidents.title: Aditi's Payovrata Vow
incidents.story: Aditi, mother of the gods, grieved to see her sons driven from heaven. Her husband, the sage Kashyapa, taught her the Payovrata, a twelve-day vow of worship living on milk alone. Aditi kept it with great devotion, and the Lord appeared before her and promised to be born as her son.
incidents.scene: Mother of gods worshipping Vishnu

incidents.title: Birth of Vamana
incidents.story: The Lord was born to Aditi and Kashyapa in his four-armed form, holding conch, discus, club and lotus. Before their eyes he became a small brahmin boy, Vamana. The sages performed his sacred thread ceremony, and the gods gave him gifts: Surya taught him the Gayatri, Brihaspati gave the sacred thread and Kubera a begging bowl.
incidents.scene: Dwarf brahmin boy receiving sacred thread

incidents.title: Vamana Asks for Three Steps
incidents.story: Vamana came to Bali's sacrifice on the Narmada, glowing like the sun. Bali welcomed him and offered any gift he wished. The boy asked only for three steps of land. Shukracharya warned that this was Vishnu himself, but Bali would not break his word, and his angry guru cursed him.
incidents.scene: Dwarf boy receiving gift from king

incidents.title: Trivikrama Measures the Worlds
incidents.story: As Bali poured water to seal the gift, Vamana began to grow until he filled the universe. With one step he covered the earth, and with the second the heavens. Brahma washed the Lord's raised foot, and that water became the holy Ganga. No room remained for the third step.
incidents.scene: Giant Vishnu striding across the heavens

incidents.title: Bali Offers His Head
incidents.story: Bound by Garuda for failing his promise, Bali stayed calm and humble. He asked the Lord to place the third step on his head. Prahlada came and praised the Lord's mercy. Pleased, Vishnu gave Bali the realm of Sutala, richer than heaven, and promised to guard his gate himself.
incidents.scene: Vishnu placing foot on king's head

incidents.title: Matsya and the Little Fish
incidents.story: King Satyavrata was offering water in the river Kritamala when a tiny fish appeared in his palms and begged for protection. He kept it in a pot, but it outgrew the pot, then a pond, then a lake. When it filled the ocean, the king knew it was the Lord himself in the form of a fish.
incidents.scene: King holding tiny fish in cupped hands

incidents.title: Matsya Saves Satyavrata's Boat
incidents.story: As the great flood rose, a boat came to Satyavrata, who boarded it with the sages, plants and seeds. A golden horned fish appeared, and the king tied the boat to its horn with the serpent Vasuki. Matsya taught him divine knowledge and saved the Vedas from the demon Hayagriva.
incidents.scene: Giant fish towing boat through flood

incidents.title: Sudyumna Becomes Ila
incidents.story: Manu longed for a son, but a mistake in the sacrifice gave him a daughter, Ila. The sage Vasishtha turned her into a man, Sudyumna. Later, hunting, Sudyumna entered a forest of Shiva where every man became a woman. As Ila again, she married Budha, son of the Moon, and bore Pururavas.
incidents.scene: Prince on horseback entering enchanted forest

incidents.title: Sukanya and the Glowing Eyes
incidents.story: Princess Sukanya, daughter of King Sharyati, saw two lights shining in an anthill and pierced them with a thorn. They were the eyes of the sage Chyavana, deep in meditation. Blood flowed, and the king's army fell ill. To make amends, Sharyati gave Sukanya to the old sage as his wife.
incidents.scene: Princess poking thorn into glowing anthill

incidents.title: The Ashvins Restore Chyavana
incidents.story: Sukanya served her old husband faithfully. One day the Ashvins, physicians of the gods, visited, and Chyavana asked them for youth. They bathed with him in a lake and three handsome youths rose alike. Sukanya chose her true husband, and in gratitude Chyavana gave the Ashvins a share of the soma.
incidents.scene: Three identical youths rising from lake

incidents.title: Kakudmi Takes Revati to Brahma
incidents.story: King Kakudmi took his daughter Revati to Brahma's realm to ask whom she should marry. Brahma laughed, for while they waited through a song, ages had passed on earth. He sent them back to marry Revati to Balarama, the Lord's own portion, now born at Dvaraka.
incidents.scene: King and daughter before Brahma

incidents.title: Durvasa's Anger at Ambarisha
incidents.story: King Ambarisha ruled the earth but gave every sense to serving Krishna. Ending a vow, he waited for the sage Durvasa to return for the meal, then sipped a little water to break his fast on time. Furious, Durvasa tore out a lock of hair and created a fiery demon to kill him.
incidents.scene: Angry sage creating fiery demon

incidents.title: Sudarshana Chases Durvasa
incidents.story: The Lord's Sudarshana discus, guarding Ambarisha, burned up the demon and then chased Durvasa. The sage fled across the worlds to Brahma and Shiva, but neither could help. At last he reached Vishnu, who said he was bound by his devotees' love, and told him to seek Ambarisha's pardon.
incidents.scene: Blazing discus chasing fleeing sage

incidents.title: Ambarisha Forgives Durvasa
incidents.story: Durvasa fell at Ambarisha's feet. The humble king prayed to the Sudarshana, and the blazing discus grew calm. Ambarisha had fasted for a whole year awaiting the sage's return, and now he fed him with honour. Durvasa praised the greatness of devotees who are kind even to those who wrong them.
incidents.scene: Sage at feet of king with discus

incidents.title: Birth of Mandhata
incidents.story: King Yuvanashva, childless, had sages perform a sacrifice for a son. At night, thirsty, he drank the sacred water meant for his queen, and he himself bore a child. When the baby cried for milk, Indra gave his finger to suck. The boy, Mandhata, grew into an emperor who ruled the whole earth.
incidents.scene: Indra feeding newborn from his finger

incidents.title: Saubhari Muni and the Fish
incidents.story: The sage Saubhari meditated under the Yamuna, but seeing fish happily mating, he wished for family life. He asked King Mandhata for a daughter, and by his powers became young and handsome, winning all fifty princesses. Later he saw that desire never ends, and returned to the forest.
incidents.scene: Sage meditating underwater among fish

incidents.title: Harishchandra's Vow to Varuna
incidents.story: King Harishchandra, childless, prayed to Varuna and vowed to sacrifice his son to him if one were born. Rohita was born, but the king kept delaying. Rohita fled to the forest, and Varuna struck the king with dropsy. Rohita then bought the boy Shunahshepa as a substitute, and the king was healed.
incidents.scene: King praying to god of waters

incidents.title: Kapila and the Sons of Sagara
incidents.story: King Sagara performed the horse sacrifice, but Indra stole the horse and left it near the sage Kapila. Sagara's sixty thousand sons dug up the earth searching for it. Finding it by the meditating sage, they insulted him, and fire rose from their own bodies and burned them to ashes.
incidents.scene: Princes burned to ashes before sage

incidents.title: Anshuman Finds the Horse
incidents.story: Sagara's grandson Anshuman followed the path his uncles had dug and found the horse beside Kapila. He bowed and praised the sage with deep humility. Pleased, Kapila returned the horse and told him that only the waters of Ganga could free his uncles, whose ashes lay heaped nearby.
incidents.scene: Young prince bowing before meditating sage

incidents.title: Bhagiratha's Penance
incidents.story: Anshuman and his son Dilipa did penance for Ganga but died before success. Then Bhagiratha performed fierce austerities, and Ganga appeared. She asked who would bear the force of her fall and how she would be cleansed of sinners' sins. Bhagiratha said Shiva would hold her, and saints would purify her.
incidents.scene: Ascetic king praying to river goddess

incidents.title: Ganga Descends to Earth
incidents.story: Pleased by Bhagiratha, Shiva caught the falling Ganga in his matted hair. Then the holy river flowed down to earth behind the king's chariot to where the ashes of Sagara's sons lay. As soon as her waters touched them, they rose to heaven, and Ganga has purified the world ever since.
incidents.scene: Shiva catching Ganga in matted hair

incidents.title: Khatvanga Attains the Lord
incidents.story: King Khatvanga fought for the gods and won. When they offered a boon, he asked how long he had to live. Told only a single hour remained, he rushed home on a flying chariot, gave up all attachment and fixed his mind on the Lord. In that brief time he reached the Supreme.
incidents.scene: King meditating after descending flying chariot

incidents.title: Rama Guards Vishvamitra's Sacrifice
incidents.story: The Lord was born as Rama, eldest son of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya, with his brothers Lakshmana, Bharata and Shatrughna. The sage Vishvamitra took young Rama and Lakshmana to guard his sacrifice. There Rama slew the demoness Tataka and drove away the demons Maricha and Subahu.
incidents.scene: Young princes with bows guarding sacrifice

incidents.title: Rama Breaks Shiva's Bow
incidents.story: At King Janaka's court stood Shiva's mighty bow, which three hundred men could hardly carry. Rama lifted it with ease, strung it and broke it in the middle, like a young elephant snapping a stalk of sugarcane. He won the hand of Sita, and on the way home humbled the proud Parashurama.
incidents.scene: Rama breaking great bow in court

incidents.title: Exile and the Loss of Sita
incidents.story: To keep his father's promise to Kaikeyi, Rama left for the forest with Sita and Lakshmana. In the Dandaka forest, Lakshmana cut off the nose of the demoness Shurpanakha. Ravana sent Maricha as a golden deer to lure Rama away, then carried off Sita to Lanka.
incidents.scene: Golden deer leading Rama into forest

incidents.title: The Ocean Bows to Rama
incidents.story: With Hanuman, Sugriva and the monkey army, Rama reached the shore. When the ocean would not make way, Rama's angry glance made its creatures tremble, and the ocean god came bearing gifts and bowed. The monkeys built a bridge of mountain peaks and trees across the sea to Lanka.
incidents.scene: Monkeys building bridge across the ocean

incidents.title: Rama Slays Ravana
incidents.story: In the great battle at Lanka, Rama killed Ravana with one arrow. He rescued Sita and returned to Ayodhya, where the people welcomed him with joy. Crowned king, Rama ruled with righteousness, and in his reign the land was free of sorrow, disease and fear.
incidents.scene: Rama shooting arrow at ten-headed Ravana

incidents.title: Nimi Lives in the Blink
incidents.story: King Nimi began a sacrifice without waiting for his guru Vasishtha, who cursed him to lose his body, and Nimi cursed him back. The sages churned Nimi's body and a son, Janaka, was born. Nimi chose not to take a new body, and was given a home in the blinking of every creature's eyes.
incidents.scene: Sages churning body to create child

incidents.title: Pururavas and Urvashi
incidents.story: King Pururavas fell in love with the heavenly nymph Urvashi, and she agreed to live with him on certain conditions. When the Gandharvas tricked him into breaking them, she vanished. Pururavas wandered mad with grief until he found her at Kurukshetra, and later won her through a sacred fire.
incidents.scene: King pleading with celestial nymph by river

incidents.title: Parashurama Defeats Kartavirya
incidents.story: The thousand-armed King Kartavirya Arjuna visited the sage Jamadagni and stole his wish-fulfilling cow. Jamadagni's son Parashurama, an avatar of the Lord, pursued him with his axe. He cut off the king's thousand arms and his head, and brought the cow and her calf back to the hermitage.
incidents.scene: Axe-wielding sage fighting thousand-armed king

incidents.title: Parashurama Obeys His Father
incidents.story: When Renuka was late returning from the river, Jamadagni ordered his sons to kill her. Only Parashurama obeyed, striking down his mother and brothers. Pleased, his father granted a boon, and Parashurama asked that they all live again. They rose as if from sleep, with no memory of death.
incidents.scene: Sage with axe before his father

incidents.title: Vishvamitra Adopts Shunahshepa
incidents.story: Vishvamitra, a king who became a brahmin sage by fierce austerity, saved the boy Shunahshepa from being sacrificed and adopted him as his eldest son. When fifty of his hundred sons refused to accept this, Vishvamitra cursed them, while the younger fifty agreed and were blessed.
incidents.scene: Sage protecting boy at sacrificial post

incidents.title: Devayani in the Well
incidents.story: Devayani, daughter of Shukracharya, quarrelled with Princess Sharmishtha after bathing, and Sharmishtha pushed her into a well. King Yayati, out hunting, pulled her out by the hand, and she asked him to marry her. Her father made Sharmishtha her maidservant, and she went with Devayani to Yayati.
incidents.scene: King pulling maiden out of well

incidents.title: Yayati and Puru's Youth
incidents.story: Yayati secretly fathered sons with Sharmishtha, and Shukracharya cursed him with old age. Still full of desire, he asked his sons to take his old age. Only the youngest, Puru, agreed. After a thousand years Yayati learned that desire is never satisfied, returned Puru's youth and sought the Lord.
incidents.scene: Old king embracing his young son

incidents.title: Bharata, Son of Shakuntala
incidents.story: King Dushyanta married Shakuntala in Kanva's hermitage, then left. She raised their son Bharata, who as a child played with lion cubs. When Dushyanta doubted the boy, a voice from heaven declared him his son. Bharata became a great emperor, and the land is named after him.
incidents.scene: Young boy playing with lion cubs

incidents.title: Rantideva Gives Away His Food
incidents.story: King Rantideva gave away all he had and lived in poverty with his family. After fasting forty-eight days, he received a little food and water. He shared it with a brahmin, a shudra, and a man with dogs, and gave his last water to a thirsty outcaste. Then the gods revealed themselves and blessed him.
incidents.scene: King offering water to thirsty outcaste

incidents.title: The Yadu Line and Krishna's Coming
incidents.story: From Yayati's son Yadu came the Yadu dynasty, in which Shurasena's son Vasudeva married Devaki. The Lord was born as their son Krishna to relieve the earth of its burden. To protect him from Kamsa, he was raised in Gokula, and his deeds purify all who hear them.
incidents.scene: Vasudeva carrying infant Krishna across river

incidents.title: Earth Pleads with Brahma
incidents.story: Burdened by armies of demon kings, Mother Earth took the form of a cow and went weeping to Brahma. Brahma led the gods to the shore of the Milk Ocean and prayed to Vishnu. The Lord's voice promised that he would soon be born among the Yadus, and the gods should take birth to serve him.
incidents.scene: Earth as cow before Brahma and gods

incidents.title: A Voice Warns Kamsa
incidents.story: At Devaki's wedding, her brother Kamsa proudly drove the bridal chariot himself. Suddenly a voice from the sky cried out that Devaki's eighth child would kill him. In a rage Kamsa seized his sister by the hair and raised his sword to cut her down on the spot.
incidents.scene: Kamsa raising sword at Devaki on chariot

incidents.title: Vasudeva's Promise
incidents.story: Vasudeva calmly reasoned with Kamsa, reminding him that death comes to every living being. Then he made a hard promise: he would hand over every child Devaki bore. Trusting his truthful word, Kamsa spared his sister, and the newlyweds went home in sorrow.
incidents.scene: Vasudeva pleading with Kamsa for Devaki

incidents.title: Kamsa Kills Devaki's Sons
incidents.story: Faithful to his word, Vasudeva brought his firstborn to Kamsa, who at first returned the child. But Narada warned Kamsa that the gods were being born among the Yadus. Kamsa threw Devaki and Vasudeva into prison and killed each of their newborn sons, one after another.
incidents.scene: Kamsa killing infant in prison cell

incidents.title: Balarama Moves to Rohini
incidents.story: When Devaki conceived her seventh child, Vishnu sent Yogamaya, his divine power, to move the baby secretly into the womb of Rohini, who lived in Gokula. The people of Mathura believed Devaki had lost the child. So Balarama, the Lord's own expansion, was born safely among the cowherds.
incidents.scene: Rohini cradling infant Balarama in Gokula

incidents.title: The Gods Praise Devaki
incidents.story: When the Lord entered Devaki's womb, she began to shine like a lamp, and even Kamsa felt afraid of her radiance. Unseen, Brahma, Shiva, Narada and the gods came to the prison and offered prayers to the Lord within her. They comforted Devaki, telling her that her son would remove the burden of the earth.
incidents.scene: Gods praying before Devaki in prison

incidents.title: Krishna Born in Prison
