incidents.story: At midnight under the star Rohini, the Lord appeared before Devaki and Vasudeva in his four-armed form, holding conch, disc, mace and lotus. The parents bowed and praised him in wonder. At Devaki's request, he then became an ordinary newborn baby, lying in her arms.
incidents.scene: Four-armed Vishnu appearing in prison

incidents.title: Vasudeva Crosses the Yamuna
incidents.story: By the Lord's power the guards fell asleep and the prison doors swung open. Vasudeva carried the baby out into a stormy night while the serpent Shesha spread his hoods as an umbrella. The swollen Yamuna parted to let him pass, and he reached Nanda's house in Gokula.
incidents.scene: Vasudeva carrying baby across Yamuna river

incidents.title: Yogamaya Escapes Kamsa
incidents.story: Vasudeva left Krishna beside sleeping Yashoda and carried her newborn daughter back to the prison. Kamsa rushed in and dashed the girl against a stone, but she slipped from his hands and rose into the sky as the eight-armed goddess. She told him his killer was already born elsewhere.
incidents.scene: Eight-armed goddess rising above Kamsa

incidents.title: Nanda's Birth Festival
incidents.story: Gokula woke to find that Yashoda had a beautiful son. Nanda bathed, gave thousands of cows to the brahmanas, and the whole village burst into celebration. Cowherds sprinkled one another with butter, milk and turmeric water, and the gopis came singing with gifts for the child.
incidents.scene: Cowherds celebrating Krishna's birth in Gokula

incidents.title: Putana Comes to Gokula
incidents.story: Kamsa sent the demoness Putana to kill newborn babies. She came to Gokula disguised as a lovely woman, and no one stopped her as she entered Nanda's house. Smiling sweetly, she lifted baby Krishna onto her lap and offered him her breast, which she had smeared with deadly poison.
incidents.scene: Putana disguised as beautiful woman nursing Krishna

incidents.title: Krishna Slays Putana
incidents.story: Krishna drank the poison along with Putana's very life. Screaming, she fell down in her true giant form, crushing trees for miles around, while the tiny baby played fearlessly on her chest. Because she had nursed him, even as an enemy, she attained the place of a mother.
incidents.scene: Baby Krishna on giant fallen demoness

incidents.title: Krishna Kicks the Cart
incidents.story: During a festival, Yashoda laid her sleeping baby under a heavy handcart. Waking hungry, Krishna kicked his little feet and the cart overturned with a crash, its pots and wheels scattered. Some say a demon named Shakata hid in the cart, and the tiny foot ended him.
incidents.scene: Baby Krishna overturning cart with foot

incidents.title: Trinavarta the Whirlwind
incidents.story: The demon Trinavarta swept into Gokula as a whirlwind, filling the sky with dust and snatching baby Krishna high into the air. Krishna grew so heavy that the demon could not fly on. Clinging to his throat, the baby choked him, and Trinavarta crashed to earth on a rock.
incidents.scene: Whirlwind demon carrying baby Krishna into sky

incidents.title: Garga Names the Boys
incidents.story: The sage Garga came secretly to Nanda's cowshed to perform the naming ceremony. He named Rohini's son Balarama for his strength, and Yashoda's son Krishna, for his dark color. Garga told Nanda that this child was equal to Narayana and would protect them from every danger.
incidents.scene: Sage Garga naming Krishna in cowshed

incidents.title: Krishna and Balarama Crawl
incidents.story: The two brothers crawled about Gokula on hands and knees, their ankle bells jingling. They followed strangers and then hurried back to their mothers in fright, splashed with mud. Holding calves' tails, they were dragged around the yard as the gopis laughed and forgot their chores.
incidents.scene: Infant Krishna and Balarama crawling in courtyard

incidents.title: The Little Butter Thief
incidents.story: As he grew, Krishna stole butter and curd from the gopis' homes, feeding the monkeys and sharing with his friends. When pots hung high, he stood on stools and broke them. The gopis came to complain to Yashoda, but seeing his innocent face, they could only smile.
incidents.scene: Krishna stealing butter from hanging pot

incidents.title: The Universe in His Mouth
incidents.story: The boys told Yashoda that Krishna had eaten dirt. When she scolded him, he denied it and opened his mouth for her to look. Inside she saw the whole universe: stars, mountains, oceans, and even Gokula and herself. Then his maya covered her vision, and she loved him as her son again.
incidents.scene: Yashoda seeing universe in Krishna's mouth

incidents.title: Krishna Tied to the Mortar
incidents.story: When Yashoda left her churning to save boiling milk, Krishna broke the butter pot and ran off. She caught him and tried to tie him to a wooden mortar, but every rope was two fingers too short. Seeing her tired and sweating, Krishna let himself be bound, and was called Damodara.
incidents.scene: Yashoda tying Krishna to wooden mortar

incidents.title: The Curse of Nalakuvara
incidents.story: Long ago Kubera's proud sons, Nalakuvara and Manigriva, were bathing drunk and naked when Narada passed by. Out of mercy, Narada cursed them to stand as twin arjuna trees in Gokula. There, he said, they would one day see the Lord himself face to face and be set free.
incidents.scene: Narada cursing Kubera's sons in river

incidents.title: The Twin Arjuna Trees Fall
incidents.story: Dragging the mortar behind him, little Krishna crawled between the twin arjuna trees. The mortar stuck sideways, and with one pull the great trees crashed to the ground. Out stepped the shining sons of Kubera, who praised Krishna and returned home freed from their curse.
incidents.scene: Krishna pulling mortar between falling trees

incidents.title: The Fruit Seller Blessed
incidents.story: A fruit seller came crying out her wares in Gokula. Krishna ran to her, carrying a little grain in his tiny hands to trade, though most of it spilled along the way. She filled his hands with fruit, and when she looked down, her basket was overflowing with jewels.
incidents.scene: Child Krishna buying fruit from woman

incidents.title: The Move to Vrindavana
incidents.story: After so many dangers, the elder Upananda advised that the cowherds leave Gokula. They loaded their carts and drove their herds to Vrindavana, a fresh land of green forests, Govardhana Hill and the sandy banks of the Yamuna. Krishna and Balarama were overjoyed and began herding calves.
incidents.scene: Cowherds with carts moving to Vrindavana

incidents.title: Vatsasura the Calf Demon
incidents.story: While the boys grazed their calves by the Yamuna, a demon disguised as a calf slipped into the herd. Krishna spotted him and walked up quietly. Seizing him by the hind legs and tail, he whirled him around and hurled him into a wood apple tree, where he fell dead.
incidents.scene: Krishna whirling calf demon into tree

incidents.title: Bakasura the Crane
incidents.story: One day the boys saw a huge crane at the water's edge, as big as a mountain peak. It was the demon Bakasura, and he swallowed Krishna whole. Krishna burned his throat like fire until he spat him out, then grabbed both halves of his beak and tore the bird apart.
incidents.scene: Krishna tearing open beak of giant crane

incidents.title: Aghasura the Python
incidents.story: Aghasura, brother of Putana and Baka, stretched himself out as a python miles long, his open mouth like a mountain cave. Thinking it was a sight to explore, the boys and calves walked straight in. Krishna went in after them and grew until the serpent burst, saving them all.
incidents.scene: Cowherd boys entering giant python's mouth

incidents.title: Lunch on the Yamuna Bank
incidents.story: Krishna and his friends sat in circles on the riverbank to share their lunch, laughing and teasing. Krishna sat in the middle, his flute tucked in his belt and a lump of rice in his hand, making jokes. The gods in the sky watched in wonder at the Lord eating with cowherd boys.
incidents.scene: Krishna sharing lunch with cowherd boys

incidents.title: Brahma Steals the Boys
incidents.story: Wishing to test Krishna, Brahma hid the calves and then the cowherd boys in a cave. Krishna simply became every calf and every boy himself, with their same faces, clothes and flutes. For a whole year the mothers and cows loved their children more than ever, without knowing why.
incidents.scene: Brahma hiding calves and cowherd boys

incidents.title: Brahma's Prayers
incidents.story: When Brahma returned, he saw the boys he had hidden and an identical group playing with Krishna. Then all the copies turned into four-armed forms of Vishnu, each worshipped by a Brahma. Humbled, Brahma fell at Krishna's feet and offered long, heartfelt prayers for forgiveness.
incidents.scene: Brahma bowing at young Krishna's feet

incidents.title: Dhenukasura the Donkey
incidents.story: The boys longed for the sweet palm fruits of Talavana, but the donkey demon Dhenuka guarded the grove. When Balarama shook the trees, Dhenuka kicked him in the chest. Balarama seized him by the hind legs and flung him onto a palm tree, and Krishna and Balarama killed his whole herd.
incidents.scene: Balarama hurling donkey demon into palms

incidents.title: Krishna Dances on Kaliya
incidents.story: The serpent Kaliya had poisoned a lake of the Yamuna, killing the cows and boys who drank there. Krishna climbed a kadamba tree and leapt into the water. Caught in Kaliya's coils, he broke free and danced on the serpent's many hoods until Kaliya vomited blood and gave up.
incidents.scene: Krishna dancing on hoods of serpent

incidents.title: Kaliya's Wives Plead
incidents.story: As Kaliya lay near death, his wives, the Naga women, came forward with folded hands. They praised Krishna and begged him to spare their husband. Krishna mercifully let Kaliya go and sent him to the island of Ramanaka, promising that Garuda would no longer harm him there.
incidents.scene: Naga wives praying to Krishna on Kaliya

incidents.title: Krishna Swallows the Fire
incidents.story: That night the people of Vraja slept by the Yamuna, worn out with worry. Suddenly a forest fire surrounded them on all sides. Terrified, they cried out to Krishna for help. The infinite Lord simply drank up the whole blazing fire and saved them all.
incidents.scene: Krishna swallowing forest fire to save cowherds

incidents.title: Pralambasura Carries Balarama
incidents.story: The demon Pralamba joined the boys' games disguised as a cowherd. Losing a match, he had to carry Balarama on his back, but instead he ran off and took his huge demon form. Calm and strong, Balarama struck the demon's head with his fist and killed him on the spot.
incidents.scene: Demon carrying Balarama on his back

incidents.title: The Song of the Flute
incidents.story: When autumn came, Krishna entered the forest with the cows, playing his flute. Hearing it, the gopis of Vraja sang of its wonder: the deer stood still, the rivers trembled, and the birds closed their eyes to listen. Their hearts went out to the cowherd boy with the flute.
incidents.scene: Krishna playing flute among cows and deer

incidents.title: The Gopis' Garments
incidents.story: The young gopis kept a month-long vow, worshipping goddess Katyayani to win Krishna as their husband. One morning, as they bathed in the Yamuna, Krishna took their clothes and climbed a kadamba tree. He returned them with blessings, promising to fulfill their wish in the autumn nights.
incidents.scene: Krishna in tree with gopis' clothes

incidents.title: The Brahmanas' Wives
incidents.story: Hungry in the forest, the boys asked some brahmanas at a sacrifice for food, but they were ignored. Their wives, however, hurried out with dishes of every kind and served Krishna with love. Later the brahmanas regretted their pride and praised the devotion of their wives.
incidents.scene: Brahmana wives bringing food to Krishna

incidents.title: Krishna Stops Indra's Worship
incidents.story: Krishna saw the cowherds preparing their yearly sacrifice to Indra, king of the gods. He told Nanda that they should worship the cows, the brahmanas and Govardhana Hill, which fed their herds. The cowherds agreed and joyfully offered their feast to the hill instead.
incidents.scene: Cowherds worshipping Govardhana with offerings

incidents.title: Krishna Lifts Govardhana
incidents.story: Furious, Indra sent clouds to pour rain and hail on Vraja for seven days. Krishna lifted Govardhana Hill with one hand like an umbrella and called everyone with their cows to shelter beneath it. He held it up for seven days without food or rest, until Indra gave up.
incidents.scene: Krishna holding hill over cowherds

incidents.title: Indra's Surrender
incidents.story: Ashamed, Indra came to Krishna in secret and bowed at his feet, begging forgiveness for his pride. Then the heavenly cow Surabhi bathed Krishna with her milk, and Indra bathed him with the waters of the Ganga. They crowned him Govinda, the protector of the cows.
incidents.scene: Indra on elephant bowing to Krishna

incidents.title: Nanda Rescued from Varuna
incidents.story: Nanda once bathed in the Yamuna in the dark hour before dawn, and a servant of Varuna, the lord of the waters, dragged him away. Krishna went to Varuna's realm, where Varuna worshipped him and returned his father. Back home, Krishna showed the cowherds a vision of his own spiritual realm.
incidents.scene: Krishna visiting Varuna's underwater palace

incidents.title: The Call of the Flute
incidents.story: On a full moon night of autumn, Krishna played his flute in the forest. Hearing it, the gopis left everything, their cooking, children and husbands, and ran to him. Krishna tested them and asked them to go home, but they wept and pleaded, and so he began to dance with them.
incidents.scene: Gopis running to Krishna on moonlit night

incidents.title: The Gopis Search for Krishna
incidents.story: When the gopis grew proud of his attention, Krishna suddenly vanished. Wild with longing, they wandered the forest asking the trees, vines and deer if they had seen him. They found his footprints beside those of one favored gopi, and then found her too, left alone and weeping.
incidents.scene: Gopis searching moonlit forest for Krishna

incidents.title: The Gopis' Song
incidents.story: Gathered on the bank of the Yamuna, the gopis sang together of their love for Krishna. They remembered his smile, his walk and his flute, and begged him to come back to them. Their song of separation has been sung by devotees ever since as the purest longing for God.
incidents.scene: Gopis singing together on river bank

incidents.title: Krishna Returns
incidents.story: Krishna suddenly reappeared among the gopis, smiling, wearing a yellow cloth and a garland. Their joy was like life returning to a body. When they asked about love, he said he hid only to deepen their devotion, and that he could never repay the debt of their love.
incidents.scene: Krishna reappearing among joyful gopis

incidents.title: The Rasa Dance
incidents.story: On the Yamuna's bank Krishna began the Rasa dance, appearing between every pair of gopis so each felt he was with her alone. Bells and bangles rang, and the gods gathered in the sky to watch. Shuka told Parikshit that hearing this pure divine play frees the heart from desire.
incidents.scene: Krishna dancing in circle with gopis

incidents.title: Sudarshana Freed from Serpent Form
incidents.story: One night the cowherds camped by the Ambika forest, and a huge serpent seized Nanda by the foot. Krishna touched the snake with His foot, and at once a shining Vidyadhara named Sudarshana rose up. Cursed by sages for mocking them, he was freed by Krishna's touch and returned to his heavenly home.
incidents.scene: Krishna touching serpent swallowing Nanda

incidents.title: Shankhachuda Is Slain
incidents.story: As Krishna and Balarama sang with the gopis on a moonlit night, Shankhachuda, a servant of Kubera, carried the women away. The brothers ran after him, and Krishna struck off the demon's head with one blow. He took the shining jewel from his crown and lovingly gave it to Balarama.
incidents.scene: Krishna chasing demon carrying away gopis

incidents.title: Krishna Slays Arishtasura
incidents.story: The demon Arishta came to Vraja as a monstrous bull, shaking the earth and goring the hills. While the cowherds fled in terror, Krishna calmly called him to fight. He seized the bull by the horns, threw him down, and tore out a horn to strike him, and the gods rained flowers.
incidents.scene: Krishna fighting huge bull by horns

incidents.title: Krishna Kills Keshi
incidents.story: Kamsa sent Keshi, a giant horse demon whose neigh shook the sky. Keshi rushed at Krishna with open jaws, and the Lord thrust His arm into the horse's mouth. His arm swelled until Keshi choked and fell dead, and Narada came to praise Krishna and foretell His coming deeds.
incidents.scene: Krishna thrusting arm into horse's mouth

incidents.title: Vyomasura in the Caves
incidents.story: While the cowherd boys played a game of thieves and shepherds, the demon Vyoma joined in disguised as a boy. One by one he stole the children away and shut them in a mountain cave behind a boulder. Krishna caught him, crushed him like a beast for sacrifice, and freed His friends.
incidents.scene: Krishna seizing demon among cowherd boys

incidents.title: Akrura Comes to Vraja
incidents.story: Kamsa sent the noble Akrura to bring Krishna and Balarama to Mathura for a festival of the bow. All along the road Akrura longed for the Lord, and on reaching Vraja he rolled in the dust of Krishna's footprints. The brothers welcomed him warmly, and he told them of Kamsa's plot.
incidents.scene: Akrura bowing before Krishna and Balarama

incidents.title: Akrura's Vision in the Yamuna
incidents.story: On the way Akrura stopped to bathe in the Yamuna. Under the water he saw Krishna and Balarama, yet the brothers were also sitting in the chariot. Then he saw Vishnu resting on the serpent Ananta, praised by sages and gods, and Akrura offered a heartfelt prayer in wonder.
incidents.scene: Akrura sees Vishnu on serpent in river

incidents.title: The Rude Washerman
incidents.story: Entering Mathura, Krishna and Balarama met Kamsa's washerman carrying fine clothes and asked him for some. The proud man refused and insulted them, so Krishna struck off his head with His hand. The cowherds dressed in the royal garments, and a weaver came forward to adorn them lovingly.
incidents.scene: Krishna and Balarama taking royal clothes

incidents.title: Sudama the Garland Maker
incidents.story: The brothers came to the house of Sudama, a humble garland maker of Mathura. He bowed down and joyfully adorned them with beautiful fragrant flowers. Pleased, Krishna blessed him with deep devotion, friendship with His devotees, and lasting prosperity for his family.
incidents.scene: Garland maker offering flowers to Krishna

incidents.title: Kubja Made Beautiful
incidents.story: On the road a young hunchbacked woman, Kubja, carried fragrant sandal paste for the king. Charmed by Krishna, she gladly anointed Him and Balarama with it. Krishna pressed her feet with His toes, lifted her chin, and straightened her body, and she stood up a lovely woman.
incidents.scene: Krishna straightening hunchbacked woman

incidents.title: Krishna Breaks the Great Bow
incidents.story: In the sacrificial arena stood a mighty bow, as huge as a rainbow, guarded by many soldiers. Krishna lifted it easily with one hand, strung it, and snapped it in the middle with a crash that filled the sky. When the guards attacked, the brothers drove them off with the broken pieces.
incidents.scene: Krishna breaking huge bow in arena

incidents.title: Kuvalayapida the Elephant
incidents.story: At the wrestling arena's gate Kamsa had placed the mighty elephant Kuvalayapida to crush the boys. Krishna dodged its trunk, played with it, and pulled it by the tail. At last He knocked it down, pulled out a tusk, and killed the beast and its driver before entering the arena.
incidents.scene: Krishna pulling tusk from mad elephant

incidents.title: The Wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika
incidents.story: In the arena Krishna faced the giant wrestler Chanura, while Balarama met Mushtika. The women of Mathura cried that it was unfair to match such tender boys with mountains of men. Yet the brothers whirled and struck their foes to the ground, and the other wrestlers fled.
incidents.scene: Krishna and Balarama wrestling giant men

incidents.title: Kamsa Is Slain
incidents.story: Furious, Kamsa ordered the cowherds driven out and Vasudeva killed. Krishna leapt onto the royal dais, seized Kamsa by the hair, and threw him down into the arena, where he died. Krishna then freed Devaki and Vasudeva from prison and restored old Ugrasena as king.
incidents.scene: Krishna dragging Kamsa from his throne

incidents.title: Study with Sandipani
incidents.story: Krishna and Balarama went to Avanti to study with the sage Sandipani, mastering all knowledge in sixty-four days. As His fee, the teacher asked for his son, lost in the sea. Krishna slew the demon Panchajana, took his conch, and brought the boy back from Yama's realm.
incidents.scene: Krishna and Balarama studying with guru

incidents.title: Uddhava's Message to the Gopis
incidents.story: Krishna sent His wise friend Uddhava to Vraja to comfort Nanda, Yashoda and the gopis. The gopis poured out their longing and spoke to a bee as though it were Krishna's messenger. Seeing their love, Uddhava prayed to be born as a blade of grass in Vrindavana.
incidents.scene: Uddhava speaking with grieving gopis

incidents.title: Jarasandha's Attacks and Dwaraka
incidents.story: Jarasandha, Kamsa's father-in-law, besieged Mathura again and again with vast armies. Seventeen times Krishna and Balarama destroyed his forces and let him go. To protect His people, Krishna had Vishvakarma build the wondrous fortress city of Dwaraka in the sea.
incidents.scene: Golden city of Dwaraka rising from sea

incidents.title: Kalayavana and Muchukunda
incidents.story: The barbarian king Kalayavana chased Krishna into a mountain cave. There Krishna's cloth lay over the sleeping king Muchukunda, who had been granted long rest by the gods. Kicked awake by Kalayavana, Muchukunda glanced at him, and the attacker burned to ashes.
incidents.scene: Sleeping king in cave burning attacker

incidents.title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini
incidents.story: Princess Rukmini loved Krishna, but her brother Rukmi wished her to wed Shishupala, so she sent Krishna a letter by a brahmana. On her wedding day, as she left the temple of Ambika, Krishna swept her into His chariot. He defeated Rukmi, and Rukmini was married at Dwaraka.
incidents.scene: Krishna lifting Rukmini into chariot

incidents.title: Pradyumna and Shambara
incidents.story: The demon Shambara stole Krishna's newborn son Pradyumna and threw him into the sea. A fish swallowed the baby and was brought to Shambara's kitchen, where Mayavati, who was Rati reborn, raised him. Grown up, Pradyumna slew Shambara and flew home with her to Dwaraka.
incidents.scene: Pradyumna fighting demon Shambara

incidents.title: The Syamantaka Jewel
incidents.story: The Sun god gave King Satrajit the dazzling Syamantaka jewel. His brother Prasena wore it hunting, but a lion killed him, and the people whispered that Krishna had taken it. To clear His name, Krishna followed the trail into the forest with the citizens.
incidents.scene: King wearing shining jewel like the sun

incidents.title: Krishna Fights Jambavan
incidents.story: The trail led to a cave where the bear king Jambavan kept the jewel, and they fought for twenty-eight days. Knowing Him as his Lord Rama, Jambavan gave Krishna the jewel and his daughter Jambavati. Back home, ashamed Satrajit gave Krishna his daughter Satyabhama too.
incidents.scene: Krishna wrestling bear king in cave

incidents.title: Narakasura Is Slain
incidents.story: The demon Narakasura had stolen Aditi's earrings and imprisoned sixteen thousand princesses. Riding Garuda with Satyabhama, Krishna broke into his fortress and cut off Naraka's head with His disc. The freed princesses all chose Him, and He married them in as many forms.
incidents.scene: Krishna and Satyabhama on Garuda in battle

incidents.title: Krishna Brings the Parijata
incidents.story: After returning Aditi's earrings in heaven, Krishna, urged by Satyabhama, uprooted the heavenly Parijata tree. Indra and the gods fought to keep it, but Krishna defeated them. He planted the fragrant tree in Satyabhama's garden at Dwaraka, where bees followed it from heaven.
incidents.scene: Krishna carrying Parijata tree on Garuda

incidents.title: Krishna Teases Rukmini
incidents.story: One day as Rukmini fanned Krishna, He teased her, asking why she had chosen a poor runaway like Him over great kings. Thinking He would leave her, she fainted with grief. Krishna lifted her tenderly, comforted her, and praised her pure and steady love.
incidents.scene: Krishna comforting fainted Rukmini

incidents.title: Usha's Dream of Aniruddha
incidents.story: Usha, daughter of the demon king Bana, saw a handsome prince in a dream and fell in love. Her friend Chitralekha painted many princes until Usha recognized him as Aniruddha, Krishna's grandson. Chitralekha flew by magic to Dwaraka and carried the sleeping prince to Usha.
incidents.scene: Chitralekha showing Usha painted portraits

incidents.title: Krishna Battles Banasura
incidents.story: Bana caught Aniruddha in Usha's rooms and bound him with serpent ropes. Krishna marched on Bana's city and fought Shiva himself, who protected Bana. Krishna cut off Bana's thousand arms but four, and at Shiva's plea spared him, and Usha and Aniruddha were married.
incidents.scene: Krishna fighting Shiva and many-armed Bana

incidents.title: King Nriga the Lizard
incidents.story: Playing in the forest, Krishna's sons found a huge lizard stuck in a dry well. Krishna lifted it out with ease, and it became a shining being, King Nriga. He told how he had once mistakenly given away a brahmana's cow, and warned all kings never to take a brahmana's property.
incidents.scene: Krishna lifting lizard from well

incidents.title: Paundraka the False Vasudeva
incidents.story: Foolish King Paundraka called himself the true Vasudeva and wore a false conch, disc and crown. He sent word that Krishna must give up His emblems. Krishna came to Kashi, met him in battle, and cut off his head with the Sudarshana disc, ending his pretence.
incidents.scene: Krishna facing king with false emblems

incidents.title: Balarama Slays Dvivida
incidents.story: The ape Dvivida, a friend of Naraka, ravaged villages and insulted Balarama on Raivata hill. He mocked Balarama's women and broke his wine pot. Balarama fought him with club and plough, and when the ape attacked with trees and stones, struck him dead with his fists.
incidents.scene: Balarama fighting giant ape on hill

incidents.title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura
incidents.story: When the Kauravas captured Krishna's son Samba for carrying off Duryodhana's daughter, Balarama came to make peace. They spoke to him with pride and scorn. Angry, Balarama hooked the city with his plough and began dragging it toward the Ganga, until they begged forgiveness.
incidents.scene: Balarama dragging city with plough

incidents.title: Narada Visits Krishna's Palaces
incidents.story: Curious how Krishna lived with sixteen thousand wives, Narada visited Dwaraka. In every palace he found Krishna, playing dice, bathing, worshipping, caring for children or advising ministers. Amazed by this wonder of the Lord's power, Narada sang His glories.
incidents.scene: Narada seeing Krishna in many palaces

incidents.title: Bhima Slays Jarasandha
incidents.story: Disguised as brahmanas, Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna asked Jarasandha for a duel. He chose Bhima, and they fought with clubs and fists for twenty-seven days. At Krishna's sign, Bhima tore Jarasandha in two, and Krishna freed the many kings held in his prison.
incidents.scene: Bhima tearing Jarasandha in two

incidents.title: Shishupala at the Rajasuya
incidents.story: At Yudhishthira's Rajasuya sacrifice, Sahadeva proposed that Krishna receive the first honour. Shishupala rose and heaped insults on the Lord. Krishna bore his abuse patiently, then cut off his head with the disc, and a light rose from his body and entered Krishna.
incidents.scene: Krishna's disc beheading Shishupala at sacrifice

incidents.title: Shalva and the Flying City
incidents.story: Shalva, Shishupala's friend, won from Shiva the flying iron city Saubha and attacked Dwaraka. Pradyumna fought him bravely. Krishna returned, saw through Shalva's magic, smashed Saubha with His club, and slew Shalva, and later He killed Dantavakra as well.
incidents.scene: Krishna attacking flying iron city

incidents.title: Balarama's Pilgrimage
incidents.story: Not wishing to take sides in the Kurukshetra war, Balarama went on pilgrimage to holy rivers. At Naimisharanya he slew the demon Balvala, who troubled the sages and rained filth on their altars. He bathed at many sacred places before returning home.
incidents.scene: Balarama with plough slaying demon

incidents.title: Sudama Visits Krishna
incidents.story: Sudama, Krishna's poor brahmana friend from school, came to Dwaraka with only a handful of flattened rice. Krishna ran to embrace him, washed his feet, and joyfully ate the humble gift. Returning home, Sudama found his hut turned into a palace, yet he stayed humble.
incidents.scene: Krishna washing poor Sudama's feet

incidents.title: Reunion at Kurukshetra
incidents.story: During a solar eclipse, the Yadavas went to bathe at Kurukshetra, and Nanda, Yashoda and the gopis came there too. After long years they saw Krishna again. Krishna embraced them, comforted them with wisdom, and their love for Him only grew deeper.
incidents.scene: Krishna meeting gopis at Kurukshetra

incidents.title: Vasudeva's Sacrifice
incidents.story: At Kurukshetra great sages came to see Krishna. Vasudeva asked them how to be free of karma, and they told him to worship the Lord with sacrifice. So Vasudeva performed a grand sacrifice, giving rich gifts, while Krishna and all the kings and gopas looked on.
incidents.scene: Vasudeva performing great fire sacrifice

incidents.title: Devaki's Six Sons Returned
incidents.story: Devaki longed to see the six sons Kamsa had killed. Krishna and Balarama went down to Sutala, where King Bali worshipped them, and brought the boys back. Devaki fed them from her breast, and touched by Krishna, the sons rose to heaven.
incidents.scene: Devaki embracing her six lost sons

incidents.title: Arjuna Carries Off Subhadra
incidents.story: Arjuna, disguised as an ascetic, stayed in Dwaraka and fell in love with Krishna's sister Subhadra. With Krishna's blessing, he carried her away in a chariot. Balarama was angry at first, but Krishna calmed him and he sent rich wedding gifts.
incidents.scene: Arjuna driving chariot carrying Subhadra

incidents.title: Shrutadeva and Bahulashva
incidents.story: Krishna went with sages to Mithila to bless two devotees, King Bahulashva and the humble brahmana Shrutadeva. Expanding Himself, He stayed in both homes at once. Each served Him with love, and Krishna praised the devotion of the brahmanas.
incidents.scene: Krishna welcomed by king and poor brahmana

incidents.title: Vrikasura and Shiva
incidents.story: The demon Vrika won a boon from Shiva that anyone whose head he touched would die. At once he chased Shiva himself to test it, and Shiva fled across the worlds. Vishnu appeared as a young brahmana student and tricked Vrika into touching his own head, and the wicked demon fell dead.
incidents.scene: Shiva fleeing demon, Vishnu as brahmana

incidents.title: Bhrigu Tests the Trimurti
incidents.story: The sages sent Bhrigu to find which of the three gods was greatest. Brahma grew angry and Shiva rose to kill him, but when Bhrigu kicked sleeping Vishnu, the Lord rose, pressed his foot, and asked pardon. Bhrigu declared Vishnu supreme.
incidents.scene: Sage kicking Vishnu's chest, Lakshmi beside

incidents.title: The Brahmana's Sons Brought Back
incidents.story: A brahmana of Dwaraka lost each of his nine sons at birth. Arjuna vowed to save the tenth but failed and nearly gave up his life. Krishna drove with him beyond the darkness to Mahakala, the abode of Vishnu on Ananta, and brought back all ten sons to the joyful brahmana.
incidents.scene: Krishna and Arjuna before cosmic Vishnu

incidents.title: Krishna's Life in Dwaraka
incidents.story: In Dwaraka Krishna lived as a householder with His queens, sporting in gardens and on lakes. His queens sang of their love for Him. He had countless sons and grandsons, and the Bhagavatam ends the Tenth Skandha praising His glorious deeds.
incidents.scene: Krishna with queens in Dwaraka gardens

incidents.title: The Sages' Curse and the Iron Club
incidents.story: Some Yadu boys dressed Samba as a pregnant woman and mockingly asked visiting sages what child she would bear. The angry sages said she would give birth to an iron club that would destroy their whole race. A club did appear, and though it was ground to powder and thrown into the sea, the curse could not be undone.
incidents.scene: Yadu boys mocking sages, Samba disguised

incidents.title: Narada Visits Vasudeva
incidents.story: The sage Narada came to Dwaraka, and Vasudeva welcomed him with honour. Though Krishna was his own son, Vasudeva humbly asked how a person could become free from fear and gain devotion. Narada smiled and answered by telling him an ancient conversation between King Nimi and nine great sages.
incidents.scene: Narada seated with Vasudeva in palace

incidents.title: Nimi and the Nine Yogendras
incidents.story: Nine brothers, sons of Rishabha and wandering sages clad only in the sky, arrived at King Nimi's sacrifice. Nimi rose and worshipped them, then asked about the true devotee, Maya, liberation and the avatars. One by one the nine Yogendras answered him, teaching that loving devotion to Hari is the surest path.
incidents.scene: nine sages before king at sacrifice

incidents.title: The Gods Ask Krishna to Return
incidents.story: Brahma, Shiva and the gods came to Dwaraka and showered Krishna with flowers and praise. They said that His work on earth was done, the burden of the earth was removed, and over a hundred years had passed. They begged Him to return to His own abode, and Krishna agreed, saying the Yadus too must now depart.
incidents.scene: gods praising Krishna in Dwaraka

incidents.title: Uddhava's Grief
incidents.story: Seeing omens of ruin, Krishna told the Yadus to go to Prabhasa. Uddhava understood that his Lord was about to leave the world, and he fell at Krishna's feet in tears. He begged to be taken along, saying he could not bear even a moment without Krishna. Moved by his love, Krishna began to teach him.
incidents.scene: Uddhava weeping at Krishna's feet

incidents.title: The Avadhuta and King Yadu
incidents.story: King Yadu once met a young, carefree Avadhuta wandering in bliss and asked the secret of his joy. The sage said he had learned from twenty four gurus in nature. From the earth he learned patience, for she bears every burden and harm and still serves all creatures without complaint.
incidents.scene: king meeting wandering naked ascetic

incidents.title: The Python's Lesson
incidents.story: The Avadhuta told how he learned from the python, which lies still and eats whatever food comes to it by chance. If nothing comes, it rests without worry, trusting fate. So a wise person does not struggle anxiously for food or comfort, but stays content and puts his strength into seeking the Lord.
incidents.scene: python lying still in forest

incidents.title: The Lesson of the Bee
incidents.story: The bee taught the Avadhuta to take a little from many flowers without harming any. So a sage gathers wisdom from every scripture and accepts only a little food from many homes. But the honeybee that hoards honey is robbed and killed, so a seeker should never store up more than he needs.
incidents.scene: bees gathering nectar from flowers

incidents.title: Pingala the Courtesan
incidents.story: In Videha the courtesan Pingala waited all night at her door for rich lovers who never came. Weary and disappointed, she suddenly felt deep detachment and saw her folly. She turned her heart to the Lord who dwells within, gave up hope in others, and slept in peace. Hope brings misery, said the Avadhuta.
incidents.scene: courtesan waiting at doorway at night

incidents.title: The Kurari Bird
incidents.story: A kurari bird carried a piece of meat, and stronger birds chased and pecked it without mercy. The moment it dropped the meat, it was left alone and happy. From this the Avadhuta learned that clinging to what others desire brings suffering, while letting go brings peace.
incidents.scene: bird chased by hawks carrying meat

incidents.title: The Girl's Bangles
incidents.story: A young girl was husking rice alone when guests came to ask for her hand. Not wanting the noise of her bangles to shame her family, she broke them one by one until a single bangle remained on each wrist. The Avadhuta learned that where many live together there is quarrel, so a seeker should live alone.
incidents.scene: girl husking rice wearing bangles

incidents.title: The Arrow-Maker
incidents.story: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in shaping his arrow that he did not notice the king's grand procession passing right beside him. From him the Avadhuta learned single-pointed concentration. When the mind is fixed firmly on the Self, the world and its distractions fade away.
incidents.scene: craftsman making arrow, royal procession passing

incidents.title: The Miserly Brahmana of Avanti
incidents.story: A rich brahmana of Avanti was so greedy that he denied comfort to himself and his family. When his wealth was lost, everyone abandoned him and people mocked and beat him as a wandering beggar. Yet he bore it calmly, saying the mind alone causes joy and sorrow, and he found peace in the Lord.
incidents.scene: beggar ascetic mocked by villagers

incidents.title: Krishna Teaches Uddhava
incidents.story: Krishna lovingly taught Uddhava about devotion, knowledge, detachment and seeing the Lord in all beings. Uddhava's doubts vanished and his heart was filled with peace. Krishna gave him His own sandals and sent him to Badarikashrama, where Uddhava lived in meditation on his Lord.
incidents.scene: Krishna instructing Uddhava, giving sandals

incidents.title: The Yadus at Prabhasa
incidents.story: At holy Prabhasa the Yadus bathed and gave gifts, then drank strong wine and lost their senses. Old quarrels flared and they fought one another fiercely. When their weapons broke, they pulled up the eraka reeds that had grown from the iron powder, and these became like iron clubs as the curse came true.
incidents.scene: Yadu warriors fighting with reeds by sea

incidents.title: Balarama's Departure
incidents.story: After the slaughter, Balarama sat in meditation on the shore of the sea. From His mouth a great white serpent emerged, the divine Ananta, and glided into the waters. So Balarama left His human form and returned to His own nature, while the ocean welcomed Him with reverence.
incidents.scene: white serpent emerging from Balarama by sea

incidents.title: Jara's Arrow
incidents.story: Krishna sat beneath a pipal tree, resting His foot on His knee, shining in four-armed form. A hunter named Jara, whose arrow was tipped with the last fragment of the iron club, mistook the reddish sole of His foot for a deer and shot. Seeing his mistake, Jara fell at Krishna's feet in terror, but was forgiven.
incidents.scene: hunter shooting arrow at Krishna's foot

incidents.title: Daruka and the Chariot
incidents.story: Krishna's charioteer Daruka came searching for his master and found Him beneath the tree. Before his eyes Krishna's chariot and divine weapons rose into the sky and vanished. Krishna told the weeping Daruka to go to Dwaraka, tell the family what had happened, and warn them that the city would be flooded.
incidents.scene: charioteer kneeling before Krishna under tree

incidents.title: Krishna's Departure
incidents.story: Brahma, Shiva and all the gods gathered in the sky to watch. Closing His eyes, Krishna fixed His mind within Himself and returned to His own abode with His form, like lightning flashing into the clouds. Drums sounded and flowers rained down, and with His going, truth and dharma left the earth.
incidents.scene: Krishna ascending, gods showering flowers

incidents.title: Arjuna and Dwaraka Sinking
incidents.story: Arjuna came to Dwaraka, performed the last rites for the departed, and led the women and children away to Indraprastha. As soon as they left, the sea rushed in and swallowed the city, sparing only Krishna's own palace. Grieving deeply for his friend, Arjuna felt that his strength had gone with Krishna.
incidents.scene: ocean flooding the golden city Dwaraka

incidents.title: The Kings of Kali Yuga
incidents.story: Shuka foretold the dynasties of the future, the Nandas, Mauryas and many others, and the rise of Kali Yuga. Kings would grow greedy, people would value wealth over virtue, and life would become short. Yet he said there is one great blessing in this age: simply by chanting the names of Hari, one is freed.
incidents.scene: Shuka speaking to king Parikshit

incidents.title: The Four Dissolutions
incidents.story: Shuka described the four kinds of dissolution. There is the daily dissolution when Brahma sleeps, the great dissolution when all creation returns to its source, and the endless dissolution of beings dying each moment. The fourth is the final one, when a soul is freed by knowledge and never returns.
incidents.scene: cosmic deluge, Vishnu resting on serpent

incidents.title: Shuka's Last Teaching
incidents.story: Shuka gave his final words to Parikshit: give up the idea that you will die, for that belongs to the body alone. You are the eternal Self, one with the supreme Brahman. A snake cannot harm the soul. Having blessed the king, Shuka rose and departed, leaving Parikshit fearless and at peace.
incidents.scene: sage blessing king by river Ganga

incidents.title: Parikshit's Liberation
incidents.story: Parikshit sat facing north by the Ganga and merged his mind in the Lord. Takshaka came disguised as a brahmana, after turning back the healer Kashyapa with wealth, and bit the king. The fire of the poison burned his body to ashes, but Parikshit had already reached the Supreme, and the gods showered flowers.
incidents.scene: serpent biting king seated in meditation

incidents.title: Janamejaya's Snake Sacrifice
incidents.story: Hearing how his father had died, King Janamejaya was furious and began a great sacrifice to burn all serpents in the fire. Thousands of snakes fell into the flames, and Takshaka fled to Indra for shelter. Brihaspati then calmed the king, saying each being meets the fate of its own deeds, and the sacrifice ended.
incidents.scene: snakes falling into sacrificial fire

incidents.title: Vyasa Divides the Vedas
incidents.story: Seeing that people of the coming age would be weak in memory and strength, Vyasa divided the one Veda into four. He taught the Rig to Paila, the Yajur to Vaishampayana, the Sama to Jaimini and the Atharva to Sumantu. Their disciples spread the Vedas far and wide through many branches.
incidents.scene: Vyasa teaching four disciples in hermitage

incidents.title: Markandeya's Tapas
incidents.story: The young sage Markandeya lived for countless years in austerity and worship of the Lord. Indra feared his power and sent Kama, the apsaras and the spring breezes to break his vow, but the sage was unmoved and they withdrew. Then Nara and Narayana appeared before him, and he prayed to see the Lord's Maya.
incidents.scene: sage meditating, apsaras dancing nearby

incidents.title: The Child on the Banyan Leaf
incidents.story: Suddenly a terrible flood covered the whole world, and Markandeya wandered for ages in the dark waters. Then he saw a banyan tree, and on one leaf lay a radiant baby sucking His toe. Drawn in by the child's breath, he saw the entire universe inside Him, then was breathed out again into the deluge.
incidents.scene: baby Krishna on banyan leaf in flood

incidents.title: Shiva and Parvati Bless Markandeya
incidents.story: Shiva and Parvati were passing through the sky and saw Markandeya deep in meditation. Parvati asked Shiva to grant him a boon. When the sage opened his eyes, he worshipped them, and Shiva blessed him with endless fame, freedom from old age and death until the end of the age, and steady devotion to Hari.
incidents.scene: Shiva and Parvati on Nandi blessing sage

incidents.title: The Glory of the Bhagavatam
incidents.story: Suta closed the great tale by praising the Bhagavatam as the essence of all scriptures. Like the Ganga among rivers and Vishnu among gods, it is supreme among the Puranas. Whoever hears or recites it with devotion is purified and finds love for Hari, the Lord who removes all suffering.
incidents.scene: sage reciting scripture to gathered sages
